item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Aaron Boone's Anthony Volpe reveal may finally stick a fork in Ryan McMahon before Yankees playoff run

item.content:encoded:
With one six-foot-seven sized caveat, the biggest concern facing the New York Yankees as we prepare for October is third base. Ryan McMahon has proven to be too much of a liability at the plate to count on as he's sunk to a new low as the only player in the league (min. 350 plate appearances) to post a sub-.280 on-base percentage and a strikeout rate north of 29%.
Meanwhile, Amed Rosario's inability to do his one job, hit lefties, and porous glove make him an untenable alternative. It appeared as if the Yankees would just have to deal with a black hole in the lineup and/or a butcher in the field, but Aaron Boone's latest update might have a solution coming to the rescue in a strange way.
With Jazz Chisholm Jr. back in action, and apparently kissing fans, the skipper announced a new plan for Anthony Volpe: playing third base. Boone always uses qualifiers, so to be accurate, he said he'd "probably" send Volpe out the man the hot corner some time this week, so there's always a chance that the frustratingly opaque manager could change his mind. Still, it would be nice to have another option, and believe it or not, Volpe could be a decent one.
Anthony Volpe ironically could come full circle and become a Yankees savior with the proposed third base plan
There's some reason to be concerned about how Volpe can handle third base, especially due to questions about his arm. The greater fear is that if he struggles there, he'll bring those issues with him to the batter's box and scuffle on the offensive side of the ball as well.
However, the former can't-miss prospect got a decent amount of run at the hot corner during his last demotion to Scranton, and during the last month he was in Triple-A, he hit 10 homers and posted an eye-popping 1.023 OPS.
Since he's come back up, his bat hasn't been that hot, hitting .263/.300/.395. Still, that's an improvement over McMahon, and he's had a few big moments over the last few weeks, most notably his September 10 grand slam against the Colorado Rockies.
Getting him some big league reps at the position before the playoffs begin is a great way to test this out in a low-pressure environment now that New York has clinched home-field advantage against the Boston Red Sox for the upcoming AL Wild Card Series.
If it works, well, it sets up a world of possibilities. We don't want to get ahead of ourselves, but Volpe getting hot at a new position in the postseason could completely flip his career narrative. If he makes a positive impact, his confidence could soar, fueling more and more encouraging developments.
At the end of it all, he could prove to be a viable replacement for the struggling McMahon this offseason. That's huge because unless the Yankees pull off a blockbuster trade, the free agent market is barren at the hot corner. One step at a time, but this could serve as the jumping-off point for Volpe's rebirth, and we're 100% here for that.

item.title: [El Imparcial] ¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026
item.dc:creator: Patrizio Caro
item.description: ¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026 El capitán de los Yankees recibió una inyección para tratar su nueva lesión. Te explicamos qué le pasó, cuándo podría regresar y cómo llegan los Yankees a los Playoffs de MLB 2026. Los New York Yankees podrían comenzar los Playoffs de MLB 2026 sin Aaron Judge. El capitán del equipo sufrió una nueva lesión en la pantorrilla derecha y recibió una inyección de plasma
item.content:encoded:
¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026
El capitán de los Yankees recibió una inyección para tratar su nueva lesión. Te explicamos qué le pasó, cuándo podría regresar y cómo llegan los Yankees a los Playoffs de MLB 2026.
Los New York Yankees podrían comenzar los Playoffs de MLB 2026 sin Aaron Judge. El capitán del equipo sufrió una nueva lesión en la pantorrilla derecha y recibió una inyección de plasma el lunes 21 de septiembre, en un intento por favorecer su recuperación antes del inicio de la postemporada.
El mánager Aaron Boone confirmó este martes que el jardinero presenta una distensión muscular moderada y que la organización está preparando la Serie de Comodines, programada para comenzar el 29 de septiembre, sin contar con él. No obstante, todavía no está descartado oficialmente.
La situación llega en un momento complicado para Judge, quien apenas había regresado de una fractura en una costilla que lo mantuvo fuera de actividad durante más de tres meses. Mientras tanto, los Yankees ya aseguraron su clasificación a los Playoffs, aunque terminaron perdiendo la División Este de la Liga Americana ante los Tampa Bay Rays.
¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge y cuál es su nueva lesión?
Aaron Judge sufrió una distensión moderada del músculo sóleo de la pantorrilla derecha el miércoles 16 de septiembre, durante el encuentro de los Yankees contra los Minnesota Twins.
El bateador de 34 años comenzó a sentir molestias desde la primera entrada, pero decidió mantenerse en el partido. Finalmente, tuvo que abandonar el encuentro en el sexto episodio y fue reemplazado por Heliot Ramos.
Al día siguiente, una resonancia magnética confirmó la lesión muscular. El sábado 19 de septiembre, los Yankees colocaron a Judge en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, con efecto retroactivo al jueves 17.
El sóleo es un músculo que se encuentra en la parte posterior de la pierna, debajo de los gemelos. Participa en movimientos fundamentales para un beisbolista, como correr, impulsarse y mantener la estabilidad.
¿Por qué le inyectaron plasma a Aaron Judge y en qué consiste el tratamiento?
La novedad de su recuperación
El lunes 21 de septiembre, durante el día de descanso de los Yankees, Aaron Judge recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas (PPP) en la pantorrilla derecha.
La inyección forma parte del tratamiento médico que está recibiendo Judge para intentar favorecer la recuperación de su lesión muscular. Sin embargo, el procedimiento no garantiza una recuperación acelerada ni determina cuándo podrá regresar a los diamantes.
Tras la aplicación, Judge permanece con actividad física limitada mientras los servicios médicos del equipo evalúan su evolución.
¿Qué otras lesiones ha sufrido Aaron Judge durante la temporada 2026?
La lesión de pantorrilla representa otro episodio en una temporada marcada por los problemas físicos del capitán de los Yankees.
A finales de abril, Judge sufrió una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla del lado derecho, aparentemente durante una jugada defensiva contra los Houston Astros. Aunque continuó jugando varias semanas, las molestias aumentaron y finalmente tuvo que detener su actividad.
El 5 de junio, los Yankees anunciaron el diagnóstico. Judge permaneció fuera de los diamantes durante todo el verano y no regresó hasta el 8 de septiembre, cuando enfrentó a los Colorado Rockies.
Su retorno duró apenas siete encuentros antes de que apareciera la nueva lesión.
Cronología de las lesiones de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Fecha | ¿Qué sucedió? |
|---|---|
| 26 de abril | Sufrió la lesión que habría originado la fractura en una costilla. |
| 31 de mayo | Disputó su último partido antes de una ausencia de más de tres meses. |
| 5 de junio | Los Yankees confirmaron la fractura por estrés. |
| 8 de septiembre | Regresó a la alineación contra Colorado. |
| 16 de septiembre | Sufrió una distensión en la pantorrilla contra Minnesota. |
| 19 de septiembre | Ingresó a la lista de lesionados de 10 días. |
| 21 de septiembre | Recibió la inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas. |
| 22 de septiembre | Boone confirmó la gravedad moderada de la distensión y expresó sus dudas sobre su disponibilidad para los Playoffs. |
¿Qué dijo Aaron Boone sobre la lesión de Aaron Judge?
El mánager de los Yankees actualizó el estado de su capitán este martes 22 de septiembre y reconoció que no espera tenerlo disponible para el comienzo de la postemporada.
Estamos planificando que no forme parte de ella".
Así explicó Boone la postura del equipo ante la próxima Serie de Comodines. Aunque no descartó definitivamente al bateador, los Yankees se preparan para afrontar los primeros encuentros de eliminación directa sin él.
El propio Judge había manifestado el sábado 19 de septiembre su deseo de estar recuperado para los Playoffs, pero reconoció que todavía no tenía respuestas sobre los plazos de su rehabilitación.
¿Cuándo volverá a jugar Aaron Judge con los Yankees?
La primera fecha en la que Judge podría ser activado es el domingo 27 de septiembre, cuando los Yankees disputarán su último encuentro de la temporada regular contra los Baltimore Orioles.
Sin embargo, esa fecha corresponde únicamente al cumplimiento del periodo mínimo de su estancia en la lista de lesionados. No significa que el jugador vaya a estar físicamente preparado para reaparecer.
La organización no ha anunciado una fecha definitiva para su regreso. Su disponibilidad dependerá de la recuperación muscular y de las evaluaciones médicas que se realicen durante los próximos días.
¿Aaron Judge jugará los Playoffs de MLB 2026?
Su participación en la primera ronda se encuentra seriamente comprometida.
La Serie de Comodines comienza el martes 29 de septiembre, solamente ocho días después de que Judge recibiera la inyección de plasma. La cercanía de ambas fechas y la gravedad moderada de la distensión explican por qué los Yankees están preparando su alineación sin el capitán.
Si Nueva York avanza a la Serie Divisional, programada para comenzar el 3 de octubre, Judge dispondría de algunos días adicionales de recuperación. Sin embargo, tampoco está garantizada su participación en esa instancia.
Por ahora, los Yankees mantienen abierta la posibilidad de su regreso durante la postemporada, pero no existe un calendario médico confirmado.
¿Cómo están los Yankees en la temporada 2026 y cuál es su situación rumbo a los Playoffs?
Clasificados a la postemporada
Los Yankees aseguraron su boleto a los Playoffs de MLB 2026 el 14 de septiembre, pero no consiguieron conquistar la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Este martes 22 de septiembre disputaron una doble cartelera contra los Tampa Bay Rays. Primero ganaron 2-0, resultado que les permitió asegurar la ventaja de local para la Serie de Comodines. Sin embargo, en el segundo encuentro cayeron 6-1 y Tampa Bay se proclamó campeón divisional.
Así quedó la División Este de la Liga Americana
Al cierre del martes 22 de septiembre
| Equipo | G | P |
|---|---|---|
| Rays (Campeón) | 96 | 61 |
| Yankees | 90 | 67 |
Los Rays aseguraron el primer sembrado de la Liga Americana, mientras que los Yankees disputarán la Serie de Comodines.
La derrota ante Tampa Bay dejó a los Yankees con cinco partidos pendientes de temporada regular. Ahora deberán concentrarse en llegar a la postemporada con su plantel recuperado y definir cómo cubrirán la ausencia de Judge.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees en la Serie de Comodines de MLB 2026?
Los Boston Red Sox son el rival que actualmente aparece en el posible cruce de primera ronda contra los Yankees.
Boston también aseguró su clasificación a los Playoffs, por lo que ambos equipos podrían protagonizar otra serie de postemporada entre históricos rivales de la División Este.
La Serie de Comodines se disputa al mejor de tres partidos. El ganador avanzará a la Serie Divisional.
Nueva York ya aseguró que será local durante esta ronda, por lo que disputará en el Yankee Stadium todos los partidos que sean necesarios. El enfrentamiento definitivo dependerá de las posiciones al cierre de la temporada regular.
¿Quién reemplazará a Aaron Judge en la alineación de los Yankees?
Heliot Ramos es una de las alternativas que Boone ha utilizado en el jardín derecho. De hecho, fue el encargado de sustituir a Judge cuando abandonó el encuentro del 16 de septiembre contra Minnesota.
El equipo también cuenta con Cody Bellinger y Spencer Jones entre sus opciones para los jardines, mientras continúa evaluando la recuperación de Trent Grisham.
En la ofensiva, los Yankees también disponen de Ben Rice y recuperaron este martes a Jazz Chisholm Jr., quien había permanecido fuera por un esguince en el pulgar derecho.
La conformación definitiva del orden al bate y del roster para la Serie de Comodines dependerá de las decisiones de Boone y de la evolución de los peloteros lesionados.
¿Cuáles son los números de Aaron Judge en la temporada 2026 de MLB?
La prolongada ausencia de Judge ha reducido considerablemente sus estadísticas con respecto a sus temporadas anteriores.
En su regreso del 8 al 16 de septiembre, el capitán de los Yankees conectó cuatro imparables en 23 turnos, incluido un cuadrangular, y produjo tres carreras. También acumuló 13 ponches durante ese periodo.
Estadísticas de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Estadística | Total |
|---|---|
| Juegos | 66 |
| Promedio de bateo | .241 |
| Porcentaje de embasado | .360 |
| Slugging | .511 |
| Jonrones | 18 |
| Carreras impulsadas | 41 |
Estadísticas hasta su última participación, el 16 de septiembre.
¿Qué sigue para los Yankees antes del inicio de los Playoffs?
Con la División Este ya definida, los Yankees deberán aprovechar los últimos cinco encuentros de la temporada regular para preparar su participación en la Serie de Comodines.
Nueva York terminará su serie contra Tampa Bay y posteriormente recibirá a Baltimore del 25 al 27 de septiembre.
Mientras tanto, Boone deberá definir su rotación abridora, evaluar el regreso de otros jugadores lesionados y decidir qué peloteros integrarán el roster de postemporada.
La primera ronda comenzará el 29 de septiembre, mientras que las Series Divisionales están programadas para iniciar el 3 de octubre.

item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK – The news about Aaron Judge’s return to the injured list was still fresh, having been announced less than an hour earlier, and already Cody Bellinger was envisioning how the Yankees could succeed in the postseason without their captain.
Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice.
“Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here to go out, win and beat anybody.”
Now they’ll have their chance to prove it.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday that Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain of his right calf and is not expected to be ready for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, which would begin on Sept. 29.
Judge’s availability for subsequent rounds, especially the AL Division Series, is also in doubt. But the Yankees need to get there first. Here are five reasons why the Yankees, lauded as pennant favorites, still can reach the Fall Classic even if Judge doesn’t return:
Dominant starting pitching
Rodón might not even draw a start in a potential Wild Card Series, standing in line behind AL Cy Young Award frontrunner Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried. Simply put, the rotation has kept them afloat.
Yankees starters have permitted two earned runs or fewer in 40 of 51 starts since July 28, including one earned run or fewer in 33 of those starts, compiling a 2.50 ERA over that span. Overall, they’ve allowed one run or fewer in 65 games, a single-season franchise record.
“We come to win every game, regardless of who is on the field,” Rodón said. “Obviously it’s tough when you don’t have the best player in the world on the field with you. I’m hopeful that he’ll be back. But … it’s just about winning games for us.”
There’s other thump
This isn’t 2022, when Judge’s 62 home runs set a single-season AL record and served as the unquestioned engine of the offense. Mostly because of the rib injury, Judge was limited to a .241 average, 18 homers and 41 RBIs across 66 games. Ben Rice shouldered much of the load, fulfilling Boone’s spring prediction of 39 homers.
Bellinger remains an impactful force, while Luis García Jr.’s increased bat speed suggests his production is sustainable despite a recent slump. Meanwhile, Heliot Ramos has shown power after a sluggish start and will be leaned upon in the playoffs against left-handed pitching.
“We know we’re capable of winning games,” said Boone, who noted the club’s 36-24 record since the All-Star break, most of which occurred without Judge. “We’ve had to play without a lot of key pieces at different points and for large chunks of this season.”
The kids are all right
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones opened eyes during the club’s recent series against the Diamondbacks, when they crushed a Statcast-calculated combined 872 feet of home runs against Corbin Burnes – big-boy blasts of 424 and 448 feet, respectively, that suggested they’re growing more comfortable in The Show.
There have been growing pains across their first months of big league activity, with Lombard committing errors in six consecutive games over one span and Jones showing the swing-and-miss that will probably always be part of his game. But the talent is real, and no one should be surprised if either rookie delivers in a big October moment.
“We really just have to play for each other; lean on each other, pass the baton,” Bellinger said. “You do your job and control what you can.”
Improving health
While Judge’s outlook is cloudy, the Yankees are slowly becoming more whole.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. was activated from the injured list between games of Tuesday’s doubleheader, restoring a dynamic presence. It has been a disappointing year overall, but Chisholm was hot at the time of his injury (18-for-46, .391). The Yanks will look for him to pick up where he left off.
Meanwhile, Anthony Volpe made the most of an opportunity in Chisholm’s absence, which could have earned him a spot on a playoff roster – especially if they go with 11 pitchers and 15 position players in the first round. Trent Grisham is thought to be in play for the playoff roster.
“Hopefully more people are able to join and make us more formidable along the way,” Boone said.
A bolstered bullpen
The Yankees’ relievers have been among the league’s best all year, but there have been concerning signs of late. Brent Headrick ranks second in the Majors with 79 appearances and has seen inconsistent velocity, for example, suggesting he could benefit from a breather once the AL East is decided. David Bednar and Paul Blackburn, meanwhile, remain sharp.
Because the Yankees would have no reason to roster five starting pitchers in October, help is on the way. Will Warren is scheduled to make one more start and then transition to a relief role, giving the ’pen an intriguing multi-inning option. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are also in the mix.
“That’s the beauty of the postseason; guys fall into different roles and a lot of times can become heroic in roles you didn’t necessarily count on at the start of the season,” Boone said.

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Rays clinch AL East, celebrate after Yankees secure home field advantage for Wild Card round

item.content:encoded:
When the Yankees retained a large chunk of their 2025 roster, they didn’t think they’d end up starting the 2026 playoffs in the same position that they did last year.
Alas, the second-place Bombers, burdened by injuries all season, officially missed out on a division title for the second straight season, as Tampa Bay clinched the American League East and a postseason bye with a 6-1 win in the second game of Tuesday’s doubleheader between the two teams. With their significantly richer rivals thwarted — the Yankees’ luxury tax payroll is $228.9 million more than Tampa’s, per Cot’s Contracts — the Rays excitedly shook hands in front of the Bronx faithful before popping bottles and lighting cigars in the visitor’s clubhouse at Yankee Stadium.
“It’s not a good feeling, for sure,” Yankees outfielder Heliot Ramos said after going 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.
“You don’t want anyone to be celebrating at your stadium,” added Max Fried, who allowed four earned runs over 6.2 innings.
It was a sour ending to a long day that began with a 2-0 victory for the Yankees, who are now 90-67 and six games behind the Rays with five games left in the regular season. That afternoon win ensured that the Yankees will have home field advantage in the Wild Card round, which begins on Sept. 29.
The likeliest scenario is that the Yankees will host the Red Sox, just as they did in last year’s Wild Card round.
The Yankees already knew that winning the division was an uphill battle coming into this four-game series against the Rays, as they needed to sweep just to keep that improbable dream alive after losing two games in Arizona over the weekend. And even with their win in Game 1 on Tuesday, the pinstripers only had a 1.8% chance of claiming the AL East, according to FanGraphs.
“You gotta give them credit,” Aaron Boone said of the 96-61 Rays on Tuesday morning. “They’ve won a ton of games this year, games that have probably been up in the air late, and they’ve come out on top. So they’ve had a great year, and they’re always a challenge to play.”
Drew Rasmussen was particularly challenging on Tuesday night, as he out-pitched Fried and didn’t permit a hit until Ramos led off the seventh inning with a double. The right-handed Rasmussen also struck out 11 while allowing one run over 6.2 innings.
With the division race over, the Yankees can now take the remainder of the week to rest key players and experiment before their likely rematch with Boston in the Wild Card round, which they expect to play without the injured Aaron Judge. If they can win that series, they’ll face the Rays again in the ALDS, a possibility that both clubs’ managers acknowledged on Tuesday night.
“This four-game series has been circled on both of our schedules for quite some time, and that’s because of so much respect that you have for the opponent,” Rays skipper Kevin Cash said. “That’s a very talented team, and we know that we could be seeing them here in another 10, 12 games.”
“Hopefully we get another crack at them in the next couple weeks,” Boone chimed in.
While the Yankees beat the Red Sox last October and won this year’s season series against them, the Wild Card round is not how they envisioned beginning the 2026 postseason after they fell short of a division title last year.
In 2025, the Yankees ended the regular season with the same record as the pennant-winning Blue Jays. However, Toronto won the season series tiebreaker between the two teams — and therefore the AL East — earned a bye in the playoffs, and defeated the Yankees in a four-game ALDS.
The Yankees last won the East in 2024. They lost that year’s World Series to the Dodgers.
The Yanks have won their division just three times since 2013, and they haven’t won a championship since 2009. However, they still believe they can end that drought after failing to secure an AL East crown.
“It kind of sucks,” Jazz Chisholm Jr. said of losing the division. “That’s what we work on all season, but it’s not the end goal for us. That end goal is the World Series, so it doesn’t really affect us here.”

item.title: [New York Post] Jazz Chisholm Jr. makes spotty Yankees return as playoff questions loom
item.dc:creator: Dan Martin; Mark W Sanchez
item.description:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. returned to what looks like a Yankees infield competition with a hit, a walk and a defensive mistake. The second baseman was activated from the injured list for the nightcap of Tuesday’s doubleheader and got the nod at second base after Anthony Volpe — who has played well at the spot in his absence — started the first game.

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. returned to what looks like a Yankees infield competition with a hit, a walk and a defensive mistake.
The second baseman was activated from the injured list for the nightcap of Tuesday’s doubleheader and got the nod at second base after Anthony Volpe — who has played well at the spot in his absence — started the first game.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Chisholm’s most memorable moment, though, was failing to cover first base on a safety squeeze in the 6-1 loss in The Bronx that helped the Rays clinch the division.
With one out and runners on the corners in the seventh inning and Taylor Walls at the plate, manager Aaron Boone said the Yankees were aware that a bunt would be coming “more often than not.”
And sure enough, Walls pushed a bunt toward first base, and Luis García Jr. charged, as he was supposed to, Boone said.
Chisholm started to run over but stopped, believing García would halt his charge and return to the base. Chisholm instead hovered by second base.
“He’s just gotta go [to first base] every time, and he knows that,” Boone said of Chisholm, who acknowledged the mistake.
“Next time, I’ll just keep going through,” said Chisholm, who was sidelined for two weeks after spraining his right thumb Sept. 8 and has returned to a team sorting out its infield with five games to go before the postseason.
Asked before the doubleheader if Volpe would continue to get time at second with Chisholm back, Boone said, “We’ll see.”
Chisholm went 1-for-3 with a single and a walk, while Volpe went 0-for-3 with three strikeouts in the 2-0 doubleheader opener. Entering play, Volpe had hit .286 with a .753 OPS in 10 games with Chisholm on the IL.
The Yankees also have to figure out third base, as Ryan McMahon is a mess on both sides of the ball.
José Caballero got the start there in the opener against Martinez and went 1-for-3 with a pair of stolen bases, with lefty-swinging McMahon in the lineup for the nightcap against Drew Rasmussen. McMahon went 0-for-2 with a strikeout and could not make a difficult play on a Nick Fortes chopper that reached McMahon on an in-between hop and went for an infield single.
Boone said he wanted to get “regular reps” for both Caballero and McMahon, who entered Tuesday just 6-for-40 with an OPS of .402 since returning from a sprained thumb Sept. 1.
Amed Rosario, signed in the offseason with the idea of playing third against lefties, has not produced in those situations this year, and the Yankees have mostly gone with Caballero and McMahon over the last three weeks.
To make room on the roster for Chisholm, Max Schuemann was optioned to the FCL Yankees.
Clarke Schmidt played catch Tuesday after experiencing cramping in his biceps while warming up during Sunday’s game against Arizona.
Boone said the team was awaiting word from doctors regarding the right-hander’s availability, but a source told The Post’s Joel Sherman that Schmidt still felt something in the area.
Another source said an IL stint isn’t out of the question as Schmidt is trying to earn a spot on the postseason roster after missing over a year following Tommy John surgery.
Ryan Weathers threw a bullpen session between games as he works to return from a left forearm strain, and Fernando Cruz (UCL) played catch.
The Yankees haven’t announced their playoff rotation, but Gerrit Cole has started the team’s first postseason game in every season in which he’s been healthy since he joined the organization in 2020.
The right-hander will start Wednesday and was asked by The Post how he would feel if Cam Schlittler got the start in the first game of a wild-card series this season.
“Fine by me,’’ said Cole, who had a similar reaction when there was discussion of having Nestor Cortes open the playoffs in 2022. “What matters is me trying to be my best. Whatever [Boone] thinks is good.”
Shop Yankees Merch
Giancarlo Stanton jogged in the outfield between games Tuesday. Stanton suffered his third calf strain of the season, and first in his left leg, over four weeks ago, and there remains no guarantee he returns this season… The Yankees have won at least 90 games eight times in the last nine years in which there’s been a full season. … The Yankees lost both ABS challenges early in Game 1 on Tuesday, as Ali Sánchez had a poor challenge catching in the top of the first and Heliot Ramos followed with an even worse challenge at the plate in the bottom of the inning.

item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday night, the New York Yankees will play the second game of their series with the Tampa Bay Rays.
They won the first (on Tuesday afternoon) by a score of 2-0.
Anthony Volpe (who started at second base) finished with three strikeouts and no hits.
UPDATE: The Yankees lost 6-1 in the second game.
Yankees Made Volpe Change Amid Chisholm Jr. News
Ahead of the second game, the Yankees announced that Jazz Chisholm Jr. has been activated off the injured list.
The Yankees wrote (via X): “Prior to Game 2 of today’s doubleheader, the Yankees made the following roster moves: • Reinstated INF Jazz Chisholm Jr. (#13) from the 10-day injured list. • Optioned INF/OF Max Schuemann to the FCL Yankees.”
The Yankees have also announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees Game 2 9/22 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF H. Ramos RF L. García Jr. 1B S. Jones CF J. Chisholm Jr. 2B G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C R. McMahon 3B M. Fried SP”
Chisholm Jr. is starting at second base, while Volpe has been removed from the lineup.
Volpe is in the middle of his fourth season with the Yankees.
He is currently batting .248 with 51 hits, two home runs, 26 RBIs, 24 runs and 11 stolen bases in 66 games this year.
Social Media Reacts To Lineup
Here’s what people were saying:
@arrocitodo: “lets seee what this night game lineup can dooooo”
@_coachtrav: “I want to see Volpe at 3B some point in the next week lol”
@GLJrEnthusiast: “This lineup with Judge in the middle of it would’ve been so special 💔”
@grinchmeritt: “I really wish they would put Jazz at 3rd and Volpe at 2nd…just to see”
@NYYPinstripes27: “Double the Baseball, Double the Fun! The Yanks look to start the series hot and sweep the day against the Tampa Bay Rays. Jazz Chisholm Jr. has been activated and will bat sixth tonight. Mad Max will toe the slab for the Yanks. First pitch is set for 7:05 PM ET. LET’S GO YANKS!!”
Gary Phillips: “Jazz Chisholm Jr. is hitting 6th in his return. #Yankees”

item.title: [tsn.ca] Rasmussen has 11 strikeouts as Rays clinch AL East with win over Yankees
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Drew Rasmussen allowed his only hit in the seventh inning and struck out 11 as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the New York Yankees 6-1 on Tuesday in the second game of a day-night doubleheader to clinch their fifth AL East title.
The Rays (96-61) secured home-field advantage throughout the American League playoffs and took their first division crown since 2021, when they won 100 games. Tampa Bay also earned AL East championships in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season along with 2010 and 2008, when the team had its first winning season after entering the league as an expansion franchise in 1998.
Yandy Díaz hit two-run single off reliever John Schreiber in the seventh and had another two-run single in the ninth for his AL-leading 175th hit. Tampa Bay opened a six-game lead over the second-place Yankees (90-67) with five to play.
In the opener, Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings as New York delayed Tampa Bay's division celebration with a 2-0 victory.
Taylor Walls started the three-run seventh with a bunt single against Max Fried (5-5) when first base was left uncovered. Ryan Vilade hit an RBI groundout in the third after Díaz’s flyball moved runners to second and third.
Rasmussen (16-5) was nine outs from joining Matt Garza as Tampa Bay pitchers with a no-hitter when he gave up a leadoff double to Heliot Ramos on his 97th pitch. Garza held the Detroit Tigers hitless at Tropicana Field on July 26, 2010.
After allowing Ramos’ hit to left field, Rasmussen got the next two outs before walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. on a full count. Kevin Kelly entered and permitted rookie George Lombard Jr.’s RBI single before retiring Austin Wells on a groundout.
Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches, 72 for strikes. He threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of 24 hitters and notched his fourth career double-digit strikeout game.
Rasmussen allowed one hit for the fourth time this year. He also yielded just one hit in six innings against the Yankees on April 12.
Cam Booser and Bryan Baker pitched an inning apiece to finish the three-hitter.
Fried allowed four runs and six hits in 6 2/3 innings.
The Yankees were held to three hits or fewer for the 13th time this year.
Up next
Tampa Bay RHP Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.38 ERA) opposes New York RHP Gerrit Cole (9-9, 3.63) on Wednesday night.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Larry Fleisher, The Associated Press

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 08:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the AL East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays (96-61) won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games.
Tampa Bay also claimed division titles in the pandemic shortened 2020 season, 2010 and 2008 and will head to the postseason as the top seed in the AL.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches and struck out New York leadoff hitter Ben Rice twice. He also struck out rookie Spencer Jones to end the fourth after allowing a walk to Cody Bellinger, who he fanned in the first inning.
The right-hander exited after walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Kelly retired Austin Wells following Lombard's hit.
Yandy Diaz drove in two runs with a single in the seventh off reliever John Schreiber. Diaz added another two-run single in the ninth. The Rays scored their first run in the third when Ryan Vilade grounded out against New York's Max Fried (5-5), scoring Taylor Walls.
Cam Booser pitched a 1-2-3 eighth and Bryan Baker put two on in the ninth before retiring Lombard to secure the division crown.
Fried allowed four runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings. The left-hander struck out four, walked two and notched 10 ground ball outs.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [fingerlakes1.com] Yankees fall to Rays in Game 2 of doubleheader as Tampa Bay clinches AL East title | Fingerlakes1.com
item.dc:creator: Facebook Com; Fingerlakes1; Kyle Evans
item.description: The New York Yankees’ American League East hopes came to an end Tuesday night as the Tampa Bay Rays defeated New York 6-1 in Game 2 of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. The Yankees won the opening game 2-0 behind eight scoreless innings from Carlos Rodón, but Tampa Bay responded in the nightcap to clinch the division and the American League’s top playoff seed. New York managed just three hits against a Tampa Bay pitching staff that followed up its Game 1 loss with a dominant performance from Dre
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees’ American League East hopes came to an end Tuesday night as the Tampa Bay Rays defeated New York 6-1 in Game 2 of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
The Yankees won the opening game 2-0 behind eight scoreless innings from Carlos Rodón, but Tampa Bay responded in the nightcap to clinch the division and the American League’s top playoff seed.
New York managed just three hits against a Tampa Bay pitching staff that followed up its Game 1 loss with a dominant performance from Drew Rasmussen. The right-hander carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning before Heliot Ramos opened the frame with a double.
Rasmussen exited after Jazz Chisholm Jr. walked with two outs. George Lombard Jr. then delivered New York’s only run with a single that scored Ramos. Rasmussen finished with one run allowed on one hit and three walks over 6.2 innings while striking out 11.
Max Fried kept the Yankees within striking distance before Tampa Bay pulled away. Ryan Vilade’s groundout gave the Rays a 1-0 lead in the third inning.
Tampa Bay added three runs in the seventh. Taylor Walls drove in Chandler Simpson with a bunt single before Yandy Díaz followed with a two-run single. Walls also scored on the play after a close call at home plate was upheld following a Yankees challenge.
Fried allowed four runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four.
The Rays added two more runs in the ninth against Ryan Yarbrough and Michael Fulmer, with Díaz delivering another two-run single.
Chisholm, activated before Game 2 after missing 12 games with a sprained right thumb, went 1-for-3 with a walk and a strikeout.
The Yankees continue their series against Tampa Bay Wednesday at 7:05 p.m. Gerrit Cole is scheduled to start against Ian Seymour.

item.title: [New York Post] Yankees lose AL East to Rays with Game 2 defeat in doubleheader split
item.dc:creator: Mark W Sanchez
item.description:
The Yankees will not accomplish the chief goal of their regular season, which will make their chief goal of the postseason harder to accomplish. That Aaron Boone’s group will have to play a best-of-three series in the wild-card round — almost certainly against the Red Sox in The Bronx and almost certainly without Aaron Judge — is discouraging for a club that sought to avoid the same precarious position that it encountered last season.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees will not accomplish the chief goal of their regular season, which will make their chief goal of the postseason harder to accomplish.
That Aaron Boone’s group will have to play a best-of-three series in the wild-card round — almost certainly against the Red Sox in The Bronx and almost certainly without Aaron Judge — is discouraging for a club that sought to avoid the same precarious position that it encountered last season.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
That Boone’s group was forced to watch the Rays clinch — and celebrate the AL East title that the Yankees made it their mission to win — on The Bronx grass sure must have added some irritation and maybe some motivation.
One year later, the Yankees will enter the postseason the same way: through the dreaded back door that adds to their World Series degree of difficulty.
The Rays celebrated a 6-1 nightcap victory and division title on Tuesday night at the Stadium, where a 2-0 Yankees matinee win simply delayed the inevitable.
In Game 157, Tampa Bay (96-61) won its first AL East championship since 2021, and the Yankees (90-67) wrapped up the top wild card for a second consecutive season.
- CHECK OUT THE LATEST MLB STANDINGS AND YANKEES STATS
After Bryan Baker induced a ground out from George Lombard Jr. to end it, Baker raised his arms in triumph and the Rays began congratulating one another while the Yankees quietly shuffled out of their own dugout.
Last year it was the Blue Jays who edged out the Yankees (through a tiebreaker), forcing Boone’s crew to sweat out a three-game set against Boston before wilting against that Toronto club, which could arrange its starting pitchers and had home-field advantage.
And so the Yankees were vocal all spring and all season that this year, they expected better.
But amid a campaign with too many lulls, too many notable injuries and not enough step-ups during those injuries, they will enter October in the same position: likely fighting the Red Sox for a chance at knocking off AL East champions that they could not solve in the regular season.
The small-market, penny-pinching Rays did not steal the division but won it decisively.
The Yankees had been playing catch-up since June 28 and never caught up. With two more now meaningless games to play, the Rays have won seven of the 11 head-to-head matchups.
For a brief glimpse at what has gone wrong this season for the Yankees, consider how they lost the nightcap:
— A team that has not hit enough without Judge again did not hit enough without Judge, no-hit until the seventh inning against Drew Rasmussen. Heliot Ramos’ double ensured the night might be embarrassing but would not be humiliating.
— A team that did not capitalize enough on its excellent starting pitching again did not capitalize enough on its excellent starting pitching. They won the opener behind eight shutdown innings from Carlos Rodón, but a slip from Max Fried in the second game was the only opening Tampa required.
Shop Yankees Merch
All it took in the third inning was an infield single, a walk, a flyout that advanced both runners and a ground out that scored the go-ahead run. The deficit would grow in the seventh because …
— A team that did not play enough clean baseball again did not play enough clean baseball. With runners on first and third and one out, Taylor Walls pushed a bunt toward first base. Fried pounced, did not believe he had a play on Chandler Simpson at home and so he looked toward first, where no one covered. First baseman Luis García Jr. had charged, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. lingered around second base.
No out was recorded in what became a three-run frame that became one more regrettable inning in a season in which the Yankees have had too many to earn a first-round bye.

item.content:encoded:
Some days, nothing can kill your vibe.
Tuesday, it would seem, was one of those for Jazz Chisholm Jr. Activated off the 10-day IL between games of the Yankees' doubleheader against the Rays, Chisholm was seeing his first action in two weeks, and his good spirits simply couldn't be contained.
Take, for example, this particular fan interaction.
While Chisholm waited on deck in the bottom of the fourth inning, a fan took the opportunity to sneak in a quick picture with the infielder from the front row. Chisholm noticed and paused his routine to pose with her. But a good day, clearly, calls for more than a standard fan selfie -- much to her amusement, Chisholm instead gave the fan a light peck on the head through the safety netting.
Of the thousands -- perhaps millions -- of player-fan selfies out there, that one may be one of a kind.

The New York Yankees secured a 2-0 victory in their series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Now, on Tuesday, they'll play the second game of a doubleheader with the Rays, just one win away from clinching the AL East division and the No. 1 overall seed in the American League.
Ahead of the matchup, Yankees manager Aaron Boone made some changes to his starting lineup as they welcome back Jazz Chisholm Jr. from the IL.
Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Move
With Chisholm Jr. coming back, Lombard Jr.'s spot in the order is seemingly dropping, at least for the second game on Tuesday.
After batting fifth in the first game of the day, Lombard Jr. will drop to seventh in the order, while Spencer Jones moves up to fifth and Chisholm Jr. bats sixth.

Lombard Jr.'s 2026 Season With Yankees
While he's only been with the team for roughly a month and a half since his Aug. 4 call-up from Triple-A, Lombard Jr. has exceeded expectations with how well he's adapted to the MLB level.
He's certainly had his hiccups along the way, but nothing has slowed him down, and he's continued to start at shortstop since the Yankees promoted him.
Lombard Jr. enters Tuesday night hitting .235 across 37 games and 132 at-bats, with 20 runs, 31 hits, five home runs, and 17 RBIs.

item.title: [blogs.fangraphs.com] Yankees Face Judge Dread
item.dc:creator: Michael Baumann

item.content:encoded:
When Aaron Judge is healthy, he’s the most dangerous hitter in baseball. Sometimes I get alarmed at how uncontroversial a statement that is; ours is a sport that so frequently humiliates those who make such sweeping, unequivocal judgments as those.
But the empirical evidence is what it is. Judge has played 150 or more games in a season four times in his career. In those four seasons, he’s led all position players in WAR four times and led the league in wRC+ three times. He’s been named AL MVP three times and finished second once, ahead of some real doozies: Cal Raleigh’s 60-homer year, Bobby Witt Jr.’s 10.5-WAR campaign in 2024, Shohei Ohtani’s best pitching season — in fact, a healthy Judge is the only thing that’s ever trumped a healthy Ohtani in an MVP race.
So again, it’s not uncontroversial to say that when Judge is healthy he’s the best hitter in the world. He has not, however, always been healthy. Least of all this season, when he missed three months with a broken rib. And now, the single-season AL home run king is back on the IL with a calf strain. The timing could not be worse.
Judge last played on Wednesday, leaving open the option to activate him on Sunday for the final game of the regular season. That seems like a theoretical concern at the moment rather than a practical one. Our Matt Martell was at Yankee manager Aaron Boone’s pregame media availability on Tuesday morning, where Boone illustrated the inadequacy of a return-to-play timeline at this point in the season.
“We’re planning on [Judge] not being a part of [the Wild Card Series],” Boone said. “You hear all the time with injuries, we give ranges: two to four weeks, four to six. They’re ranges for a reason. We’re at a point in the year where, obviously, we’d push it a little bit if that was in play, but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either.”
That’s the problem. A range of two weeks in recovery time isn’t a big deal in a six-month season, but even one week is twice as long as the Yankees’ entire first playoff round. And muscle injuries can be finicky to begin with — you go to bed one night feeling fine and wake up the next morning with weakness or stiffness.
For what it’s worth, the Yankees are technically still alive in the AL East race as of this writing, but you can forgive Boone for speaking as if the division is already lost.
Either way, in order to speed things along, Judge received a platelet-poor plasma (PPP) injection on Monday, not to be confused with a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection.
Now, apparently having read The Magic School Bus Inside the Human Body as a child is not a sufficient qualification to perform surgery on live patients. At least, that’s what the police told me. But anyone who’s read that book can tell you the makeup of human blood: Red blood cells, which carry oxygen; white blood cells, which fight infection; platelets, which stop bleeding and heal wounds; and plasma, which is the broth all the other stuff floats around in.
PRP injections are a pretty common treatment for sports injuries, but taking the healing bits out of plasma seems kind of counterintuitive. Sort of like a vodka-poor screwdriver. But evidently PPP contains high levels of fibrinogen, which is itself a healing agent. Ms. Frizzle didn’t cover fibrinogen, but sure, I’ll buy it.
Unless the PPP works an actual miracle, though, it looks like the Yankees are going to have to navigate at least the first round of the playoffs without their best player.
And even if Judge does return — either in the Wild Card round or later, if the Yankees advance — I’d caution against assuming that we’d be seeing the best of him right off the proverbial bat. For starters, 99% of star athletes in history are going to try to force their way into the lineup for the playoffs regardless of whether they’re actually healthy.
To say nothing of the fact that Judge can be streaky. This is the nature of Judge’s unusual skill set; there are 1,073 hitters in major league history with at least 5,000 career plate appearances. Judge is the only one of those who’s produced one of the three true outcomes (home run, strikeout, walk) in more than half of his career plate appearances. (I’d like to express my immense gratitude to Adam Dunn, who has a career TTO% of 49.9, for making this fun fact possible.)
Living on the extremes, as he does, Judge will have weeks where he homers every night, and others where he goes 1-for-20 with 12 strikeouts. But you live with it because, over a long enough timeline, it works out heavily in his favor. Among hitters with at least 5,000 career plate appearances, Judge has the third-highest career wRC+, trailing only Babe Ruth and Ted Williams. If you wanted to go further than “best hitter now” and anoint Judge the best hitter ever, leaning heavily on the argument that quality of competition increases over time, you’d have a credible case.
But that’s not what the Yankees got out of Judge this year. In 66 regular-season games, he’s hit .241/.360/.511, with his highest strikeout rate (29.8%) since 2019 and lowest wRC+ (141) since 2020. In seven games since he returned from his rib injury, Judge was just 4-for-23 with one home run, one walk, and 13 strikeouts.
I’ve done enough of these injury reaction posts to figure out that they’re not really about the guy who got hurt, but about the teammates he’s leaving behind.
And I don’t want to underrate the value of Judge — even the version of Judge that has a 141 wRC+, rather than a 200 wRC+ — but the Yankees have done OK without him.
In the weakest American League field in decades, the Yankees are one of only two teams with a winning percentage of .550 or better. Entering their doubleheader with the Rays on Tuesday, the Yankees are still first in the AL in home runs (216) and second in runs scored per game (4.60). Even without Judge (or Giancarlo Stanton, for that matter), their lineup has plenty of beef.

Ben Rice in particular has been absolutely terrific this season. He’s fourth among qualified AL hitters in wRC+ and third in both home runs and runs scored. The Astros have AL MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez in their lineup; apart from him, is there any hitter in the AL bracket who’s been Rice’s equal this year? Maybe Junior Caminero? Willson Contreras, if you value OBP over raw power? Even if you’re being charitable, it’s a short list.
Now, past Rice, things get interesting, because if you want to talk about the Yankees’ offensive depth, you have to be able to hold multiple ideas in your head at once.
As of Tuesday morning, the Yankees have 11 hitters with double-digit home runs this season, which is tied for the most in the league. That’s just counting players who have hit 10 or more home runs in pinstripes, and the Yankees brought in substantial reinforcements midseason. Luis García Jr. has just seven homers for the Yankees but 30 overall. Heliot Ramos has four home runs in 32 games and 13 overall, with 20-plus in each of his previous two seasons. George Lombard Jr. has just five home runs in 37 major league games, but he hit 12 dingers in 78 minor league games before he got called up.
Count all this up and the Yankees have more hitters with at least decent pop than they can fit on the roster at once.
At the same time, Rice is the only Yankee with 20 home runs in pinstripes this year. So while this lineup is short on automatic outs, if Judge is out, there’s a massive drop-off after Rice.
If you take Judge out of the picture, Cody Bellinger is second on the Yankees in wRC+, at 119. The Rays don’t have anyone with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Rice this season, but they have four hitters (Caminero, Yandy Díaz, Jonathan Aranda, and Victor Mesa Jr.) with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Bellinger. So do the Rangers (Justin Foscue, Josh Jung, Joc Pederson, Wyatt Langford). The Astros have Alvarez, plus Isaac Paredes and Jeremy Peña. The White Sox have Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami, and Tristan Peters.
As good as Rice has been, the Yankees’ lineup looks concerningly pedestrian without Judge. If you aren’t already a FanGraphs Member, please consider becoming one; it’s the only way to get trenchant original analysis like this.
The good news is that Judge’s calf injury runs counter to the rest of the team’s injury luck. Carlos Rodón, who missed almost three months with an elbow injury earlier this year, dominated the Rays in eight scoreless innings in Game 1 of a doubleheader on Tuesday. The same day, the Yankees activated Chisholm, who’d spent two weeks on the IL with a sprained thumb. Clarke Schmidt just returned from Tommy John surgery last week, and while he suffered biceps cramping in the bullpen on Sunday, it appears to be a minor setback. Trent Grisham remains a question mark for the start of the playoffs as he recovers from a hamstring injury, but his prognosis also looks good.
Judge is as important to the Yankees as any two or three other players put together, but with a healthy and deep rotation and Rice leading the way offensively, they’re not in bad shape. The remainder of this roster could easily survive and advance through a weaker AL bracket, setting the stage for a dramatically timed Judge return in mid-October. Like Kirk Gibson, only bigger.
Michael is a writer at FanGraphs. Previously, he was a staff writer at The Ringer and D1Baseball, and his work has appeared at Grantland, Baseball Prospectus, The Atlantic, ESPN.com, and various ill-remembered Phillies blogs. Follow him on Twitter, if you must, @MichaelBaumann.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees utility player Jose Caballero will get the start today at third base in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Caballero (age 30) is a former Tampa Bay Ray who was traded to the Yankees at last year's MLB trade deadline. Caballero is hitting a .236 batting average with 14 home runs, 51 RBIs, 32 stolen bases, and a .665 OPS.
Ryan McMahon Yankees Dilemma
This is an interesting development, considering third baseman and left-handed hitter Ryan McMahon has been struggling significantly lately, both offensively and defensively.
This season, McMahon is hitting .208 with 10 home runs, 35 RBIs, and a .618 OPS. McMahon's throws from third base this year have been concerning at times as well. Caballero is an above-average defender and could provide more value offensively than McMahon is right now, so it makes sense why the Yankees are trying Caballero at third base in game one of the doubleheader today against Tampa.
Yankees Getting Ready For Playoffs
With the playoffs (Wild Card) just a week away, with game one beginning Tuesday, September 29th, now is the time for the Yankees to not only rest some key players but also try guys at different positions as they figure out how the postseason roster will ultimately shake out.
The Yankees are also still waiting on the return of Jazz Chisholm Jr., which raises another question: what do the Yankees do when it comes to playing either Anthony Volpe or Jazz Chisholm Jr. at second base, and what happens to the other?
Caballero has talked about trying to provide extra spark/energy to prove himself when playing for his former squad in Tampa. The Yankees will hope to see that effect from a different position in game one of the doubleheader and in this series as they look to wrap up the regular season on a positive note. In contrast, Tampa is looking for a win to clinch the AL East Division, with the winner in a likely wild-card race between the Yankees and Red Sox then going on to face Tampa Bay.
But how Caballero fares today at third base could offer a glimpse into the Yankees' postseason strategy as they prepare for the Wild Card round, which will be no easy task after navigating the AL East. It will also be interesting to see how much this move affects Ryan McMahon's playing time for the rest of the regular season and then the postseason, unless they view it as rest for McMahon.

item.title: [fansided.com] Projecting the Yankees Wild Card series lineup after brutal Aaron Judge's injury update
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postsea
item.content:encoded:
It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postseason series is a long shot at best.
A "moderate grade" calf strain is serious enough for Yankees manager Aaron Boone to proceed as if his best player won't be active at all for the Wild Card series. That is an insanely difficult blow for a Yankees team that, with Judge, is as good as any in a weak American League. For the Yankees to advance to the ALDS and potentially get their captain back, they'll need to rely on this projected lineup below.
What the Yankees lineup could look like without Aaron Judge
Judge is an instrumental piece in the Yankees' lineup for a couple of reasons. First, he's the best hitter in the sport when healthy. That obviously matters. Second, Judge is one of the few right-handed bats on this roster. He provides much-needed balance that, without Judge, the Yankees lack.
| Position | Player |
|---|---|
| Ben Rice | DH |
| Cody Bellinger | LF |
| Heliot Ramos | RF |
| Luis Garcia Jr. | 1B |
| Spencer Jones | CF |
| George Lombard Jr. | SS |
| Jazz Chisholm Jr. | 2B |
| Austin Wells | C |
| Jose Caballero | 3B |
This lineup still has some good pieces in it. Ben Rice has had a breakout year, Cody Bellinger is a well-rounded star, and trails only Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong, the AL and NL MVP favorites, with a .532 slugging percentage. If Jazz Chisholm Jr. can return from the IL looking like the player he's capable of being, the Yankees can score runs.
The problem, though, is that six of the nine hitters in this lineup are left-handed, and most of them are much better against righties than lefties. The Yankees will use guys like Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario against left-handed pitching, but having Heliot Ramos, who has a .672 OPS since being acquired by the Yankees at the deadline, in the No. 3 hole against righties isn't ideal. The Yankees don't have much of a choice with Judge out, though.
Ultimately, with Judge out, this is a team heavily reliant on lineup platoons. It'll be on Aaron Boone to try to push the right buttons in order to get this offense, which has been remarkably inconsistent without Judge, to score runs against (likely) a potent Boston Red Sox pitching staff.
Aaron Judge injury update: Can the Yankees expect their star to return?
What's most frustrating about the Judge injury update is that we have no idea what the injury is. The Yankees, for whatever reason, keep information regarding injuries, particularly to Judge, extremely close to the vest, making it difficult to know when or even if Judge will be back. All we know is that Judge is dealing with what Aaron Boone deems a "moderate" strain.
That doesn't sound good, especially for a player who has had trouble with the same right calf in the past. In the shortened 2020 season, Judge attempted to return from a calf strain in a couple of weeks, but wound up re-aggravating the injury, pushing his return back several weeks. Calf injuries and other soft-tissue ailments are not to be messed with, and can lead to a major setback if rushed through.
Plus, if the injury was minor, wouldn't the Yankees be quick to tell the world that? I'd love to say Judge is a lock to return at some point, but even if the Yankees were to advance to the ALDS, given how little we know and how tricky returns can be from calf injuries, it's probably wishful thinking to assume he'd be back right at the start of a potential ALDS, which is the last thign any New York fan wants to hear.

item.title: [saratogian.com] Yankees Notebook: Jazz Chisholm to return for Tuesday’s night game; Clarke Schmidt avoids disaster
item.dc:creator: James Oconnell
item.description: A flurry of injury news came across for the battered and bruised Bronx Bombers on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. While the team is clearly compromised and will likely be missing their best player, Aaron Judge, when the playoffs start on Sept. 29, they will be getting their second baseman back with some time to get ready for the inevitable Wild Card Series vs. the Boston Red Sox. Jazz Chisholm Jr. is expected to be activated between games on Tuesday as the Bombers begin their four-game set with the T
item.content:encoded:
A flurry of injury news came across for the battered and bruised Bronx Bombers on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
While the team is clearly compromised and will likely be missing their best player, Aaron Judge, when the playoffs start on Sept. 29, they will be getting their second baseman back with some time to get ready for the inevitable Wild Card Series vs. the Boston Red Sox.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is expected to be activated between games on Tuesday as the Bombers begin their four-game set with the Tampa Bay Rays with a day-night doubleheader. Chisholm Jr. has been out since Sept. 8 with a right thumb sprain.
“He should be in a good spot and ready to go,” said manager Aaron Boone. “He’s been hitting now for several days and and throwing the last three or four days, so he should be ready to go.”
The 28-year-old is slashing .232/.312/.403 with 19 homers and 55 RBI in 134 games this season. The impending free agent is expected to resume duties as their starting second baseman, which likely doesn’t bode well for Anthony Volpe’s playing time.
“Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job,” said Boone. “But looking forward to getting Jazz back as well. So, Jazz, I plan on playing Jazz at second in the night game.”
Volpe has performed well since being recalled from Triple-A on Sept. 10, slashing .286/.324/.429 with a homer, seven RBI and four stolen bases. It remains to be seen how he will be utilized and if a platoon scenario between Volpe and Chisholm Jr. is on the table.
CLARKE GOOD
Clarke Schmidt appears to have avoided anything major after experiencing bicep soreness while warming up during Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
“Clark is gonna play catch [Tuesday]. He did have some testing and it looks like he’s in a pretty good spot.” Boone said. “But [he’s] gotta throw and see how he is, and then we’ll go from there. … He’s on the active roster for now, but he’s got to play catch and do all those things and see how available he is.”
Schmidt returned from Tommy John surgery on Sept. 16 against the Minnesota Twins. He is expected to play a crucial role out of the bullpen in whatever time the Yankees have in the postseason.
WEATHERS UPDATE
Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain) will throw a side session between games on Tuesday. Weathers exited his start against the Toronto Blue Jays on Aug 22 after feeling discomfort and has not appeared in a game since.
If the southpaw is to return in the postseason, it will very likely be out of the bullpen.

item.title: [MLB.com] Judge se perdería la Serie del Comodín por distensión “moderada” en la pantorrilla
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch
item.description: NUEVA YORK -- Aaron Judge tiene una distensión de “grado moderado” en la pantorrilla derecha y probablemente se pierda al menos el inicio de la postemporada de los Yankees, según el manager Aaron Boone, quien dijo que el club no planea tener a su capitán activo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas. “Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso”, dijo Boone el martes. “Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco
item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK -- Aaron Judge tiene una distensión de “grado moderado” en la pantorrilla derecha y probablemente se pierda al menos el inicio de la postemporada de los Yankees, según el manager Aaron Boone, quien dijo que el club no planea tener a su capitán activo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas.
“Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso”, dijo Boone el martes. “Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco si eso estuviera en juego. Pero falta una semana para eso. No lo espero, pero tampoco lo descarto”.
Los Yankees han asegurado un pase a la postemporada, pero los Rays pueden amarrar el título del Este de la Liga Americana y el sembrado Nro. 1 de la L.A. con una victoria en cualquiera de los choques de la doble cartelera del martes, lo que obligaría a Nueva York a disputar la Serie del Comodín.
Judge fue ingresado a la lista de lesionados de 10 días el sábado, retroactivo al 17 de septiembre.
Recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas en la pantorrilla derecha durante el día libre del lunes y tendrá actividades limitadas durante los próximos días.
“El par de días siguientes no habrá mucho: nada de correr, saltar, cosas así”, indicó Boone.
Durante la serie del club el fin de semana en Phoenix, Judge y Boone fueron vagos sobre la gravedad de la lesión, la cual Judge sufrió durante la serie de la semana pasada frente a los Mellizos.
Judge reveló que la distensión es en el músculo sóleo de su pantorrilla derecha, el cual dijo “es un poco más crucial al correr y batear”.
“He lidiado con distensiones antes y de alguna manera he jugado con ellas, pero esta fue en un lugar diferente donde lo hizo un poco más difícil”, comentó Judge.
Generalmente, una distensión de pantorrilla de Grado 2 toma de tres a seis semanas para recuperarse.
“Si él es capaz de jugar, entonces le daremos esa oportunidad”, señaló Boone.
Judge se perdió la mayor parte del verano con una fractura en la costilla derecha, que se cree sufrió el 26 de abril en Houston. Jugó con la lesión antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados a principios de junio.
Activado en septiembre sin una asignación de rehabilitación en liga menor, Judge disputó sólo siete compromisos después de ser activado, bateando de 23-4 (.174) con un jonrón. En general, Judge bateó .241/.360/.511 con 18 bambinazos y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos esta campaña.
“Hemos jugado gran parte del año sin él, y en su mayor parte, hemos hecho un trabajo bastante bueno”, destacó Boone. “Obviamente, siempre quieres a tu mejor jugador disponible. Pero entendemos que tenemos un trabajo que hacer y una expectativa de ganar. Creo que esa expectativa no cambia, con o sin él”.
En otras actualizaciones de lesiones, Boone dijo que los Yankees tienen la intención de activar al infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. entre los encuentros de la doble cartelera del martes.
El derecho Clarke Schmidt se sometió a estudios de imagen tras necesitar acortar su calentamiento el domingo en Phoenix debido a una molestia en su bíceps derecho.
“Por ahora está en el roster activo, pero tiene que soltar el brazo y hacer todas esas cosas para ver qué tan disponible está”, declaró Boone.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees facing questions about their infield heading into MLB playoffs
item.dc:creator: Peter Sblendorio
item.description: For the third time in five such games, lefty-swinging Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon was out of the lineup against a right-handed starter to open Tuesday’s doubleheader. In all three instances, righty-swinging José Caballero started at third base instead. Manager Aaron Boone chalked Tuesday afternoon’s decision up to Tampa Bay Rays starter Nick Martinez having reverse splits — meaning he’s actually tougher against lefties — and said McMahon would start the nightcap against a more traditional
item.content:encoded:
For the third time in five such games, lefty-swinging Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon was out of the lineup against a right-handed starter to open Tuesday’s doubleheader.
In all three instances, righty-swinging José Caballero started at third base instead.
Manager Aaron Boone chalked Tuesday afternoon’s decision up to Tampa Bay Rays starter Nick Martinez having reverse splits — meaning he’s actually tougher against lefties — and said McMahon would start the nightcap against a more traditional righty in Drew Rasmussen.
That would also allow the sure-handed McMahon to play defense on a night Max Fried, who regularly elicits grounders to third base, was starting for the Yankees.
But as McMahon continues to struggle, this is a trend to watch with the MLB postseason rapidly approaching.
“I want to be playing them both and getting them both regular reps,” Boone said before Tuesday’s first game, “so [it was] more just picking what game I wanted to play Caballero.”
Entering Tuesday, McMahon was hitting just .150 with a .402 OPS and no home runs since Sept. 1, when he returned from the injured list for a left thumb sprain.
Overall, he is batting .208 with 10 homers and a .618 OPS.
While his season-long numbers against right-handed pitchers (.639 OPS) are superior to his stats against lefties (.518 OPS), McMahon’s offensive production has been modest either way.
Caballero was already the preferred third-base option against left-handed starters, but now he’s seeing more playing time there against right-handers, too.
A utilityman by trade, Caballero began Tuesday with a .237 average, 10 home runs and a .676 OPS against right-handed pitching.
Caballero’s previous two starts against right-handers came on Sunday against Arizona’s Corbin Burnes, whose splits are fairly even for his career, and last week against Minnesota’s Bailey Ober, who is better against righties than lefties.
That means Caballero isn’t only getting chances against right-handed pitchers with reverse splits.
And while McMahon’s calling card is typically his glove, the advanced metrics have not been favorable to the 31-year-old this season.
McMahon entered Tuesday with -1 Defensive Runs Saved and 1 Outs Above Average — down considerably from his 10 DRS and 7 OAA in 2025.
His numbers at third base this year are comparable to those of Caballero, who began the day with 0 DRS and -1 OAA.
Caballero is also much more dynamic on the bases, as he began the doubleheader with 32 stolen bases. However, starting Caballero eliminates the ability to use him as a pinch-runner — an element of his game that makes him a valuable late-inning weapon come October.
Third base isn’t the Yankees’ only infield position with some uncertainty.
Since being replaced at shortstop by George Lombard Jr. and recalled from Triple-A, Anthony Volpe has performed admirably as the Yankees’ second baseman.
The righty-hitting Volpe began Tuesday hitting .286 with a .753 OPS since being recalled on Sept. 10. He had been worth 1 DRS and 1 OAA at second base over that small sample, too.
Volpe is not going to supplant second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was set to be activated for the second game of the doubleheader after a short IL stint for a right thumb sprain.
But Volpe could challenge for playing time at second base against left-handed pitching, against whom he is hitting .240 with a .680 OPS in the majors this season.
The lefty-swinging Chisholm has endured a down season against lefties, batting .221 with a .654 OPS and a team-worst 35% strikeout rate in those matchups.
“Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job,” Boone said, “but looking forward to getting Jazz back as well.”
The 28-year-old Chisholm wasn’t thrilled last year when the Yankees sat him against left-handed Boston Red Sox ace Garrett Crochet in Game 1 of their Wild Card series.
But with the Yankees likely to face the lefty-heavy Red Sox in the Wild Card round again next week, Boone and company will have more decisions to make at second and third — especially because offense would be at a premium if Aaron Judge (calf) can’t return in time.

Entering Tuesday’s action, he had hit safely in six of his 10 games since being called back up from Triple-A, adding a home run and seve
item.content:encoded:
BRONX, NY — Jazz Chisholm Jr. is set to be activated from the 10-day injured list following the first game of the Yankees’ doubleheader on Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
The second baseman missed two weeks after spraining his thumb, and his spot was filled in admirably by Anthony Volpe — the cast-off shortstop who has enjoyed a minor renaissance, of sorts. Entering Tuesday’s action, he had hit safely in six of his 10 games since being called back up from Triple-A, adding a home run and seven RBI. Five of them came in his first game back on Sept. 10 against the Colorado Rockies.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that Chisholm is “in a good spot” after hitting and throwing over the past several days. How playing time will shake out remains to be seen.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job, but looking forward to getting Jazz back as well.”
With the opportunity for playing time seemingly available at third base with Jose Caballero, Ryan McMahon, and Amed Rosario in the mix, Boone had said that “we’ll see” when asked about Volpe potentially moving to the hot corner. Volpe said he has yet to have those conversations with team brass.
It has been a down season for Chisholm, who owns a .715 OPS with 19 home runs and 55 RBI. After a 30/30 season last year, he came into the 2026 campaign hoping to make a run at 50/50.
That did not happen, but getting a healthy Chisholm back who could possibly recapture last year’s spark would provide a significant boost for the Yankees, who are facing the very real possibility of being without Aaron Judge for their Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox next week.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Boone shared a more positive update on Jazz Chisholm Jr. ahead of the series opener against the Rays on Tuesday.
The Yankees infielder is to be activated between games of the doubleheader and is expected to return to the lineup for the second game against Tampa Bay. Chisholm Jr. initially landed on the injured list approximately two weeks ago with a right thumb sprain.
He was always expected to return for the postseason, but it will certainly be exciting to see him get some reps before all the chaos begins. Missing Aaron Judge from the Wild Card series, the Pinstripes will need all the power they can get to gain some momentum on offense. This also raises some key questions about who will be put where in the infield once the postseason comes along.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Should Keep Jazz Chisholm Jr. at Second Base Over Anthony Volpe
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
item.description: It was easy for everybody to get ahead of themselves when Anthony Volpe had a big first game back against the Colorado Rockies. Jazz Chisholm Jr. had just gone down, and Volpe delivered a three-hit night capped by a grand slam. At that point, Volpe had gone through a torrid home run streak in the minors, so the thought was that if he replicated it in the big leagues, maybe he could usurp Chisholm. While Volpe's teammates at Triple-A saw the version of him that closely resembled an infield Barry
item.content:encoded:
It was easy for everybody to get ahead of themselves when Anthony Volpe had a big first game back against the Colorado Rockies. Jazz Chisholm Jr. had just gone down, and Volpe delivered a three-hit night capped by a grand slam. At that point, Volpe had gone through a torrid home run streak in the minors, so the thought was that if he replicated it in the big leagues, maybe he could usurp Chisholm.
While Volpe's teammates at Triple-A saw the version of him that closely resembled an infield Barry Bonds, he just wasn't that after that first game. Since then, Volpe has gone 7-for-33. He didn't hit a home run and had just two doubles in that span. In many ways, his .226/.263/.290 slash line is about where he has always been as a big leaguer.
That is why, since Chisholm will be playing in the second game of Tuesday night's doubleheader vs. the Rays, per Chris Kirschner of The Athletic, there's no reason to debate who takes second base. The answer is easily Chisholm. Chisholm hasn't had the best season, but in the postseason, he's more of a threat at the plate and on the basepaths. Chisholm has 19 homers this year with 40 stolen bases. Overall, he's hitting .232/.312/.403 at the plate.
Then, of course, there's the defense. That's why a hitter who's been at or below a 100 wRC+ all year can post a 3.2 WAR, according to FanGraphs. This year, Chisholm also has 12 Outs Above Average at the position, per Baseball Savant.
It does feel like Chisholm is the priority, too, once he's back. According to manager Aaron Boone, when asked about Volpe's status and the possibility of him playing at third base, the focus was on getting Chisholm back.
"We'll see," Boone said of Volpe getting reps at the hot corner, according to the New York Post's Greg Joyce. "First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we'll figure it out as the week unfolds, how I want to play it."
Potential infield configuration against a lefty
If the Yankees face a tough lefty in October and aren't too keen on playing Ryan McMahon, who has a 74 wRC+, and Chisholm, they might have a choice here. They could stick with Chisholm at second and have either Jose Caballero or Anthony Volpe play third base.
They could also have Chisholm go back to third base and have Volpe at second. That way, they keep the better player on the field while also getting a righty at second or third.
With Aaron Judge out, Chisholm could boost the lineup. He's had a tough year, but a big October could make up for some regular-season woes.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.
