Before the series began, Yankees manager Aaron Boone announced major news
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MAY 18: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees reacts after hitting a two-run home run during the seventh inning against the Toronto Blue Jays at Yankee Stadium on May 18, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images)
The New York Yankees are set to begin a four-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday.
Before the series began, Yankees manager Aaron Boone announced major news involving second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who has been on the injured list since Sept. 10 with a sprained right thumb.
New York Yankees’ Aaron Boone Announces Jazz Chisholm Jr. News Before Tampa Bay Rays Series
Chisholm said he will play in Game 2 of Tuesday’s doubleheader, according to multiple reports.
GettyANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 01: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees reacts after hitting a solo homerun during the first inning of a game against the Los Angeles Angels at Angel Stadium of Anaheim on September 01, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images)
Chisholm is set to be a free agent at the end of the season.
The second baseman has had a rough year at the plate for his standards, slashing .232/.312/.403 over 134 games.
GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 23: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees looks on during the second inning against the Toronto Blue Jays at Yankee Stadium on August 23, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)
FanGraphs and Baseball Reference value Chisholm much differently.
He has been worth 1.5 bWAR and 3.4 fWAR this year.
GettyANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 01: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees is late with a tag on Oswald Peraza #2 after a single hit by Tyler Heineman #31 of the Los Angeles Angels during the fifth inning of a game at Angel Stadium of Anaheim on September 01, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images)
Chisholm began his MLB career with the Miami Marlins in 2020.
Miami traded him to New York during the 2024 season.
GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 12: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees in action during the game against the Seattle Mariners at Yankee Stadium on August 12, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. The Yankees won 10-5. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)
In his three seasons with the Yankees, Chisholm has posted a .774 OPS with 61 home runs and 158 RBI.
In his seven-year MLB career, the second baseman has posted 14.1 bWAR, 17.8 fWAR and a .245/.315/.445 slash line. He has 127 home runs, 363 RBI and 170 stolen bases throughout his career.
Game 1 of the doubleheader between the Yankees and Rays is scheduled to begin at 1:05 p.m. EDT. The second game will begin at 7:05 p.m. EDT.
Jackson Kruse Jackson Kruse covers Major League Baseball for Heavy Sports. He is also the site expert for FanSided's Minnesota Twins site, Puckett's Pond, and writes for Nolan Writin', FanSided's Texas Rangers site. Jackson earned a Bachelor of Science in Electronic Media from Texas State University's School of Journalism and Mass Communication. Before joining Heavy Sports and FanSided, he served as sports editor of The University Star, Texas State University's student-run newspaper. More about Jackson Kruse

item.content:encoded:
Yankees' playoff picture, Aaron Judge update and potential rotation
This wasn’t how the Yankees wanted to move into the regular season’s final week, with a four-game set against Tampa Bay.
Beginning with Tuesday’s day-night doubleheader, they’ll need to sweep the AL East leaders just to prevent the Rays from spilling champagne inside Yankee Stadium’s visiting clubhouse.
And there’s uncertainty surrounding Yankees captain Aaron Judge’s availability next week – the start of postseason − due to a right calf strain.
“We’ve been through a lot as a team this year already and we’ve answered the bell at mostly all the turns,’’ Yanks manager Aaron Boone told reporters, including the YES Network, after Sunday’s 8-4 loss at Arizona.
“(We’re) looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason.’’
Here’s a look at the Yankees’ week ahead:
Yankees vs Rays with AL East race nearing its end
In winning 12 of their last 15 games, the Rays (95-60) have opened a six-game divisional lead on the Yanks (89-66).
On the verge of its first AL East title since 2021, Tampa Bay could clinch it with one win on a long Tuesday in the Bronx.
Tuesday’s opener has Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) scheduled to oppose lefty Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95), with righty Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) vs. lefty Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the nightcap.
The Yanks are scheduled to start Gerrit Cole on Wednesday and Cam Schlittler on Thursday.
In the wider picture, Boone acknowledged the need to prep for next week, which includes giving important bullpen arms like Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn some added rest.
“You’ve got to make sure guys are in a good spot going in (to postseason),’’ Boone told reporters, speaking generally on Sunday.
“But we’re going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday.’’
Aaron Judge injury update
Judge’s availability for the first playoff round remains a mystery.
This past weekend, Judge told reporters: “I’d like to be back by the postseason. That’s definitely the plan.’’
Judge said he’s played through minor calf strains before, but this current injury to the soleus muscle is a more problematic spot.
So, this will be a key week of treatment and testing to see if Judge could be available in any capacity for a first-round playoff series.
Yankees injury news as Jazz Chisholm Jr. might return
Sidelined since Sept. 9, lefty-hitting second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (right thumb sprain) could be activated from the injured list to start the Tampa Bay series.
Though he’s unlikely to be activated this week, lefty reliever Ryan Weathers (flexor strain) could find himself on a playoff roster next week in a bullpen capacity.
On the IL since Sept. 5, center fielder Trent Grisham (strained right hamstring) has progressed in his running and is also a possible postseason choice.
Recovered from Tommy John surgery rehab, right-hander Clarke Schmidt developed cramping in his right biceps area while warming up Sunday.
Schmidt did not enter the game, telling reporters it was “more precautionary…especially with the playoffs coming up,’’ in what could be an important relief role.
Initial testing revealed no shoulder or elbow issues, but Schmidt planned to be examined by the team physician Monday.
Schmidt called it “frustrating,’’ but feels “in the grand scheme, we’ll be out there soon.’’
How Yankees' playoff rotation might look
With the likelihood of the Yanks hosting a best-of-three Wild Card series beginning Tuesday, they'd have Cam Schlittler ready on regular rest vs. Boston in Game 1.
But that might not be how the Yankees set things up.
Gerrit Cole would be on one extra day of rest if he's the Game 1 choice, or the Yanks could give the ball to Max Fried with nearly a full week of rest. It's been one month since Fried's return from a second elbow bone bruise this season.
Carlos Rodon could be on a Wild Card roster in an emergency or long relief capacity, or he might be saved to start Game 1 or 2 of a best-of-five Division Series.
CC Sabathia to be honored at Yankee Stadium
Prior to Saturday night's game against the Orioles, CC Sabathia's No. 52 will be retired in a ceremony at Yankee Stadium.
He'll be the 24th Yankees player or manager so honored and the first since Paul O'Neill, who had his No. 21 retired in August 2022.

item.title: [New York Post] Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s imminent return will push Yankees to make difficult lineup decisions
item.dc:creator: Greg Joyce
item.description:
Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s return from a right thumb sprain is near, meaning the Yankees face some interesting decisions. The second baseman could be activated from the injured list as soon as Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Rays, and while the corresponding roster move appears simple (Max Schuemann), the potential lineup moves bear watching.

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s return from a right thumb sprain is near, meaning the Yankees face some interesting decisions.
The second baseman could be activated from the injured list as soon as Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Rays, and while the corresponding roster move appears simple (Max Schuemann), the potential lineup moves bear watching.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
After Chisholm got hurt diving into second base Sept. 8, the Yankees called up Anthony Volpe to get some run at the position he had mostly transitioned to at Triple-A, and he made the most of it.
In the 10 games since Volpe was recalled, he has started at second base nine times (José Caballero started the other) and mostly looked sharp, batting .286 with a .753 OPS and four steals.
Whether Volpe has done enough to warrant at-bats once Chisholm returns remains to be seen. Shortly before he was called back up, the natural shortstop had also started to mix in some third base, starting three games there, though Aaron Boone would only offer, “We’ll see,” when asked whether that could be an option for Volpe with Chisholm back.
“First things first, getting Jazz back and then we’ll figure it out as the week unfolds how I want to play it,” Boone said.
The Yankees have not gotten much offensive production from their third basemen this year, especially of late. Since returning from his own thumb sprain Sept. 1, Ryan McMahon has hit just 6-for-40 (.150) with a .402 OPS, with Caballero starting at third over him Sunday against a righty. Amed Rosario has often started at third against lefties, and while he has not hit in line with his career numbers, the Yankees continue to believe he will.
Boone could also platoon Volpe and Chisholm at second base, as the lefty-hitting Chisholm is batting only .221 with a .654 OPS against lefties. But the pending free agent had just been starting to get hot in a disappointing season, hitting .391 with a 1.028 OPS over his last 15 games before getting hurt.
If and where Volpe fits on the playoff roster is just one of the many decisions they will have to consider over this final week of the regular season.
“You know it’s going to take a lot of players and a lot of people when you get to spring training and the season unfolds,” Boone said. “We’ll have hopefully some tough decisions to make when we’re setting postseason rosters and things like that. But that’s a better problem to have.”
Shop Yankees Merch
Clarke Schmidt was expected to see the team doctor early this week after experiencing biceps cramping while warming up Sunday, which kept him from entering the game. The right-hander had just made his return from Tommy John surgery and is trying to carve out a role in the playoff bullpen.
Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain) could also have a role in a playoff bullpen, but first the lefty will need to face hitters this week as he tries to show the Yankees he could jump right into postseason action without pitching in a game since he got hurt Aug. 22.

item.content:encoded:
We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.

| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |

It was a great week for the Brewers. They won their fourth straight NL Central title and sixth in the last nine years, and also set another franchise record for wins in a single season, one year after setting the previous record. They now have a chance to win 100 games for the first time in club history this week and still have the top seed in the NL to play for.
The Rays swept the Athletics and won their series against the Red Sox last week to put some distance between themselves and the Yankees in the AL East race. The gap in the division is now six games, and even though the two rivals play each other four times during the final week of the season, it would take a massive collapse from Tampa Bay to upset the current standings. Because the Rays also currently lead the season series with the Yankees, 6-3, all they need is to win one of the four games in New York to take the division title. With Shane McClanahan still recovering from his forearm injury — his availability for the playoffs is up in the air — Freddy Peralta has stepped up to lead the pitching staff over the last few weeks. Across his last five starts, he’s allowed just three runs in 28 2/3 innings. That’s the kind of production the Rays were hoping to get when they acquired him at the trade deadline.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dodgers | 96-60 | 1580 | 1492 | 100.0% | 1621 |
| Padres | 87-69 | 1578 | 1501 | 97.2% | 1618 |
| Braves | 92-64 | 1565 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1610 |
| Yankees | 89-66 | 1556 | 1497 | 100.0% | 1603 |
The Dodgers are getting all their pieces in place for the postseason. Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki will be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and Shohei Ohtani should follow on Wednesday. There’s a lingering question about Blake Snell’s status after he injured his groin last week, but it sounds like he’ll be able to make a start during the final weekend of the season. And even though the majority of the year has been a slog for Kyle Tucker, his bat seems to have finally woken up at the right time; he collected nine hits and three home runs last week.
Having won 13 of their last 14 games, the Padres are peaking at exactly the right moment. They’ve surged five games ahead of the Diamondbacks and one ahead of the Phillies in the NL Wild Card standings, and are now tied with the Cubs for the top spot. San Diego’s final series of the season against Arizona still looms large, especially if the Friars stumble against the Dodgers in the series beforehand. You’re probably familiar with Fernando Tatis Jr.’s hot streak — he blasted four home runs last week to bring his total in September up to eight — but the biggest contributor to the Padres’ success recently has been Ty France. He had 12 hits and a home run last week and has posted a fantastic 168 wRC+ during the second half of the season.
After a couple of years away from the top, the Braves are NL East champions again — it’s their seventh division title in the last nine years. Atlanta’s dominance this year has been a welcome return to form. Even though his season has been a bit up and down, Ronald Acuña Jr. is looking like the superstar that won the MVP back in 2023 again. Last week, he smacked three home runs, including a go-ahead grand slam on Saturday, and is running a 191 wRC+ in September.
A little more than a week after being activated off the IL, Aaron Judge is back on the shelf, this time with a calf injury sustained on Wednesday. His availability for the playoffs is still up in the air, though he’s confident that he’ll be able to return sooner rather than later. Thankfully, Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and there’s some confidence that Trent Grisham will also be ready to return for the postseason. It helps that Ben Rice has bounced back from a rough August to post a 192 wRC+ in September. Still, Judge’s injury is a major blow to the Yankees’ hopes for a deep October run.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red Sox | 84-72 | 1544 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1594 |
| Phillies | 86-70 | 1546 | 1501 | 97.3% | 1593 |
| Cubs | 87-69 | 1539 | 1501 | 99.9% | 1590 |
Even though the Red Sox lost both of their series last week, they managed to clinch a postseason berth on Sunday. It’s the cap to a remarkable turnaround after the team looked completely lost in mid-June. Boston can officially secure the second Wild Card spot with a couple of wins against the Guardians this week. Then the team can turn its attention to the Yankees and the rematch of last year’s Wild Card matchup between these two historic rivals.
Nothing is going to come easy for the Phillies over the next few weeks. The team placed Jesús Luzardo on the IL last week with a shoulder injury, but thankfully, it sounds like he’ll be ready to pitch in the playoffs. But before they count their chickens, they need to actually clinch a playoff spot. Philadelphia is four games up on the Diamondbacks in the NL Wild Card race, but its upcoming opponents are no cake walk; the Phillies have the Brewers and Rays on the schedule to finish off the regular season. Facing two of the best teams in baseball is quite a test ahead of the postseason, and the Phillies haven’t exactly been playing well lately.
The biggest concern for the Cubs right now is the status of Alex Bregman. He was struck by a foul ball in the face while standing in the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game and was taken to the hospital for further evaluation. Alongside Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been one of the best hitters in baseball since the All-Star break. It would be a huge blow if the third baseman had to miss any significant amount of time at this point in the season. As for Crow-Armstrong, he’s two stolen bases away from joining the 40/40 club. He put a few finishing touches on his MVP case last week by bopping four more home runs, bringing his season total up to 45.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guardians | 81-75 | 1520 | 1498 | 97.6% | 1572 |
| White Sox | 80-76 | 1494 | 1500 | 96.2% | 1552 |
| Rangers | 78-78 | 1502 | 1496 | 56.5% | 1517 |
| Astros | 77-79 | 1493 | 1493 | 45.8% | 1481 |
There was some upheaval in the two division races represented in this tier. Entering last week one game behind the White Sox in the AL Central standings, the Guardians took two of three games against the South Siders in a dramatic series, which included a walk-off on Tuesday and an improbable go-ahead homer on Wednesday. From there, although Chicago took advantage of playing — and winning — on Thursday while Cleveland was off to pull back into a tie atop the division, the Guardians just kept winning, sweeping the the Athletics over the weekend to bring their winning streak to five. José Ramírez finally broke out of his extended slump, tallying nine hits, a home run, and four stolen bases last week.
As for the White Sox, they won three of their four games against the the Tigers, but that one loss was enough to drop them to a game behind Cleveland in the Central. Still, the Sox have a three-game cushion for the final AL Wild Card spot, and they own the tiebreaker over the Guardians, meaning both first place and a potential first-round bye are still in their sights. Miguel Vargas is carrying most of the load for the lineup right now, hitting three home runs last week, but he needs some support if Chicago wants to make some noise in the postseason.
Over in the AL West, the Astros were swept by the Braves this past weekend, allowing the Rangers to jump into first place with a .500 record. Texas enters this week one game up, but crucially Houston holds the tiebreaker. If the Rangers can manage to hang on, it would be just their second postseason appearance in the last decade. The last time they made the playoffs, they won the World Series.
The Houston bullpen was responsible for the backbreaking losses on Saturday and Sunday, but the lack of offense has been a much bigger problem. Over the Astros’ last 10 games, they’ve scored more than four runs in a game just once. Yordan Alvarez looked fine last week (eight hits, including two home runs) after his ankle scare the previous weekend, and Jeremy Peña has been great too (10 hits, three homers), but the rest of the lineup has been struggling. During this 10-game stretch, Houston hitters not named Alvarez or Peña have combined for an ugly 55 wRC+.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diamondbacks | 82-74 | 1527 | 1505 | 5.6% | 1464 |
| Blue Jays | 77-79 | 1516 | 1504 | 3.6% | 1456 |
The Diamondbacks managed to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a pair of wins over the Yankees on Saturday and Sunday. The first victory was a walk-off and the second was highlighted by a go-ahead grand slam from Nolan Arenado. Arizona needs to take care of business in Colorado and get some help from the Dodgers to ensure that the final series against the Padres has some stakes. There’s a chance the Phillies could crash out, opening another window for the Snakes, but the direct path is through San Diego.
The Blue Jays’ hopes for a last-minute surge into the playoffs were dashed last week when they lost both of their series to the Tigers and Rangers. They’re three games back and have the Astros to contend with if they want to try and sneak into that final Wild Card spot. It’s probably too little, too late, but the team is activating Trey Yesavage off the IL on Monday as one more reinforcement ahead of a final push.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pirates | 79-77 | 1534 | 1509 | 0.0% | 1465 |
| Mets | 71-85 | 1508 | 1509 | 0.0% | 1446 |
| Orioles | 75-81 | 1493 | 1504 | 0.1% | 1435 |
| Marlins | 76-80 | 1476 | 1503 | 0.0% | 1422 |
| Tigers | 73-83 | 1470 | 1491 | 0.0% | 1417 |
| Reds | 72-84 | 1469 | 1508 | 0.0% | 1416 |
The series between the Orioles and Mets last week in Queens turned out to be more interesting than you’d expect from two teams mired in hugely disappointing seasons. Pete Alonso made his first appearance as a member of the opposing team at Citi Field and wound up hitting his 300th career home run on Tuesday, a game-tying shot in the ninth inning. He received a huge ovation from the hometown crowd, which drew some irksome comments from a few Mets players and staff after the game. Baltimore wound up sweeping New York to cut its deficit in the AL Wild Card race to 2.5 games. Alas, a sweep by the Brewers over the weekend slammed the door shut on any playoff hopes the O’s still had.
Even though the Marlins’ season essentially ended with that 12-game losing streak back in July, they have made some significant progress in their quest to become a contending club. Otto Lopez looks like a star they can build the lineup around, while Eury Pérez and Max Meyer should be strong enough to anchor the pitching staff in the years ahead. There’s also a cohort of young prospects in the upper minors who should be making their debuts soon. The future in Miami is brighter than it’s been in a while.
This is the huge step forward the Reds were hoping to see from Elly De La Cruz. In September, he has blasted seven home runs, including in five straight games earlier this month, and is running a major league-best 236 wRC+. It’s too bad the rest of Cincinnati’s roster is a bit of a mess. Sal Stewart has been excellent as De La Cruz’s sidekick, but the starting rotation has struggled mightily, and the big injury to Hunter Greene has thrown the ceiling of that group up in the air heading into next year. Still, building around a superstar like De La Cruz should make things easier if the resources to improve the rest of the roster are made available.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Royals | 67-89 | 1458 | 1498 | 0.0% | 1408 |

The AL Central crown runs through Kansas City; both the White Sox and Guardians travel to face the Royals during the final week of the season. Unfortunately, the Royals haven’t been playing well enough recently to act as a spoiler. They ended August with a 13-3 stretch, but they’ve been the worst team in the AL in September, with just five wins in 18 games.
It took a lot longer than expected, but the Twins were finally eliminated from the playoff race last week. It was a drama-filled week, too. They won a wild extra-inning walk-off affair against the Yankees on Wednesday and then were walked-off twice against the Angels between two shutout victories over the weekend. Even though they all made their big league debuts over the last few weeks, Walker Jenkins, Kaelen Culpepper, and Emmanuel Rodriguez never all appeared in a game together. That trio represents the future of the organization, so it’s a little disappointing that that future couldn’t be realized in a small way this year.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Joe Girardi suggests position change for Jazz Chisholm Jr. heading into playoffs
item.dc:creator: Adam Zagoria
item.description: With Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially coming off the injured list on Tuesday, former Yankees manager Joe Girardi is suggesting a position change heading into the postseason. item.content:encoded:
With Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially coming off the injured list on Tuesday, former Yankees manager Joe Girardi is suggesting a position change heading into the postseason.
Anthony Volpe now seems entrenched at second base, but Girardi, the last man to lead the Yankees to a World Series in 2009, thinks there's another position for which Chisholm, who has been out with a right thumb sprain, would be suited.
Asked by reporters if he would move Volpe over to third base with the playoffs approaching, manager Aaron Boone said, "We'll see."
"I would think that you would possibly move Jazz over there [to third base] because Jazz has done it," Girardi said on the YES Network during the Yankees' 8-4 loss Sunday to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
"He swung the bat pretty well over there, too," Girardi added. "It didn't seem to phase the offensive part of his game."
Last season, Chisholm played 29 games at third base with a fielding percentage of .920. This season, he has yet to play a game at third.
A year ago, Chisholm batted .242 with 31 home runs, 80 RBIs, 31 stolen bases and an .813 OPS.
MORE BY ADAM ZAGORIA
This year, Chisholm is batting .232 with 19 homers and 55 RBI and a .715 OPS.
Third baseman Ryan McMahon, a left-handed hitter, has been struggling offensively. The Yankees started right-handed hitting Jose Caballero on Sunday against right-handed starter Corbin Burnes.
"Caballero's had a good [road] trip, had a good night last night," Girardi said. "He can get really hot...and can do a lot of different things. I think you gotta play him."

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Varias latas de cerveza fueron vaciadas sobre la cabeza de Aaron Judge mientras el capitán de los Yankees permanecía en el centro del clubhouse de visitantes en el Target Field la semana pasada, rodeado de compañeros eufóricos que celebraban la clasificación del club a la postemporada.
Judge entrecerró los ojos por el ardor y les advirtió a sus compañeros: “Me las van a pagar”.
Aun así, no pretenden que ésa sea su última celebración, pues tienen un firme control del primer puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana y el título del Este de la Liga Americana todavía está en juego.
“Siempre es bueno cuando puedes celebrar esos momentos durante una temporada”, dijo el manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone. “Mucha gente dedica mucho tiempo, esfuerzo y sudor. Obviamente, éste es apenas el primer paso de lo que esperamos sean muchos”.
Ahora que aseguraron su pase a la postemporada, ¿qué más les espera a los Yankees?
¿Cómo podría quedar el roster para la postemporada?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez 
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos
BD: Ben Rice
LA: Gerrit Cole, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried
R: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber, Will Warren, Carlos Rodón
Los Yankees utilizaron a 12 lanzadores y a 14 bateadores cuando recibieron a los Medias Rojas en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, así que partiremos de esa misma premisa para el 2026.
Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles contra Tampa Bay, mientras que Schlittler lo hará el jueves. Mirando hacia adelante, eso sugiere que Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Es posible que los Yankees estén alineando a Cole para abrir el Juego 1 y a Schlittler para el Juego 2. Hasta ahora, han preferido no decir mucho al respecto, salvo por la confirmación de Boone de que Cole realizará una apertura en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Rodón podría estar en el bullpen para la serie. En nuestra proyección del roster lo tenemos activo, mientras que el dominicano Luis Gil y Ryan Yarbrough figuran entre quienes quedarían fuera. Ryan Weathers trabaja para regresar como relevista, pero el tiempo juega en su contra. Si está saludable, podría ocupar el lugar de Fulmer o Schreiber.
Chisholm espera regresar esta semana para la serie contra los Rays tras sufrir un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Grisham ha mostrado mejoría y podría quedarse con un puesto en los jardines. De no ser así, Max Schuemann está entre las alternativas. Otro aspecto para seguir: ¿Podrían los Yankees incluir a Anthony Volpe en lugar de Rosario? Es una posibilidad que vale la pena considerar.
¿Cuándo comenzará la postemporada?
Si los Yankees terminan disputando la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, ésta empezará el 29 de septiembre. La Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana arrancará el 3 de octubre.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees si la temporada terminara hoy?
En estos momentos, sería una revancha de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, con los Yankees recibiendo a los Medias Rojas en el Bronx. Los Yankees ganaron aquella serie dos victorias por una.
Este año, los Yankees tuvieron marca de 7-6 contra Boston.
¿Todavía pueden ganar el Este de la Liga Americana?
Sí, pero tienen un camino cuesta arriba. Los Yankees tienen por delante cuatro enfrentamientos directos con los Rays a partir del martes en el Yankee Stadium, incluyendo una doble-cartelera para abrir la serie. Tampa Bay domina actualmente la serie particular por 6-3, lo que significa que los Yankees necesitarían barrer para quedarse con el criterio de desempate entre ambos.
¿Quién abriría el Juego 1 por los Yankees?
Como se mencionó anteriormente, Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles frente a Tampa Bay y Schlittler lo hará al día siguiente. Por lo tanto, Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Después de permitir siete jonrones en sus dos aperturas anteriores, Cole mermó las dudas externas sobre una posible apertura en los playoffs con una sólida actuación en Arizona. Fried y Rodón han lidiado con lesiones, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado.
Warren realizará una apertura más durante la serie contra los Orioles, según Boone, pero llegará a los playoffs como una interesante alternativa para el relevo.
¿Será Judge un factor en los playoffs?
Los Yankees han sido poco específicos sobre el estado de Judge. Boone ha evitado ofrecer un plazo estimado para su recuperación e incluso revelar el grado del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha. En términos generales, hasta un tirón de Grado 1, el de menor gravedad, requiere de dos a tres semanas para una recuperación completa.
Es casi seguro que Judge intentará regresar antes. La primera fecha en la que podría ser activado sería para el Juego 162, el 27 de septiembre. Tal como está el panorama ahora mismo, existe una posibilidad muy real de que los Yankees no cuenten con Judge al menos para una potencial Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Judge dijo que le “gustaría” estar activo para la postemporada y que ése es “el plan”, pero no dijo necesariamente que sería para el 29 de septiembre.
¿Cuáles son las otras preocupaciones en cuanto a lesiones?
Grisham ha avanzado en su programa progresivo de correr y debe de estar disponible para el roster de los playoffs, aunque Boone dijo que no será activado antes de que termine la temporada regular. Chisholm ha estado bateando y realizando tiros, y debe de ser activado durante la serie contra los Rays. Si sufre algún contratiempo, Volpe entraría en consideración.
Y aunque los Yankees no han descartado a Giancarlo Stanton, quien ha estado bateando, han ofrecido pocas novedades sobre su recuperación del más reciente tirón en la pantorrilla.

September 21 Notes
Falling off: Aaron Judge (ninth), Dylan Cease (40th), Alex Bregman (43rd), Andrés Muñoz (71st), Jesús Luzardo (93rd), Troy Melton (117th), Bryce Eldridge (140th) and 36 other players.
- It’s a fool’s errand, but here’s one last update for the final week of the season. I tried emphasizing two-start starters unless they’re particularly dangerous, but I also tried to take into account that some of the guys currently in line to start twice are going to end up being scratched or making only brief appearances next weekend.
- With no updates yet on Alex Bregman (face) and Andrés Muñoz (knee), I’ve dropped both from the rankings. Pedro Ramírez, who was set to fall off the list with Dansby Swanson back, reclaimed a spot in Bregman’s place. Seranthony Domínguez seems like the likeliest choice for saves in Seattle in Muñoz’s place, so he comes in at No. 166.
- Thank you so much to everyone who has followed along all season. Anyone interested in the full spreadsheet of where players have ranked start to finish, reach out to my gmail at matthewpouliot. I’ll be back in mid-October with the first (or second) go at a 2027 Top 300.
September 14 Notes
Falling off: Shohei Ohtani DH (eighth), Rafael Devers (41st), Jazz Chisholm Jr. (58th), Bryce Miller (177th), Gleyber Torres (183rd), Hayden Wesneski (206th), Royce Lewis (214th), Kyle Bradish (222nd), Michael McGreevy (243rd), Brandon Pfaadt (246th), Braxton Ashcraft (250th) and 21 other players
- I don’t have much of a notes section for you right now, since it’s after 3 am and I’d like to get some sleep. Still, the rankings are updated for the final 14 days of the season. A lot of the pitcher movement this week is elevating guys with three starts remaining and dropping those with only two. I also gave Rockies hitters a nice boost, as they play 10 of their remaining 13 games at home. Padres hitters also got a little lift from that, as they’ll be starting a four-game series in Coors Field on Monday.
September 7 Notes
Falling off: Kyle Harrison (101st), Shane McClanahan (125th), Luis Robert Jr. (163rd), Trent Graham (180th), Joe Musgrove (192nd), Byron Buxton (202nd), Cam Smith (219th), Brendan Donovan (227th), JJ Wetherholt (236th), Eric Lauer (243rd), Jesús Sánchez (247th), Xavier Edwards (254th), Sean Manaea (261st), Samuel Basallo (262nd), Nathan Eovaldi (265th), Connor Norby (268th), Chase Burns (273rd), Shohei Ohtani SP (280th), Tommy White (282nd), Daniel Palencia (285th), Colton Cowser (286th), Taylor Ward (289th), Ezequiel Tovar (290th), Alek Thomas (292nd), Willi Castro (294th), Elvis Alvarado (295th), Brandyn Garcia (299th)
- With three weeks to go, nearly every injured player is off the rankings at this point, with the exception of a few guys hopefully returning before the end of this week. Also, I’m paying a lot more attention to matchups, particularly this week’s. So, some starters with multiple starts this week who wouldn’t normally be in the top 300 make the cut. Also, Athletics hitters have moved up, since they’ll be at home for six games this week. Rockies hitters have dropped off as that team goes back on the road after a week of home games.
- Rafael Devers gets an overdue late bump. There really was good reason for concern early on with his strikeout rate up and his bat speed down, but he bounced back nicely in both categories. Amazing is the consistency in his wOBAs since 2021: .373, .373, .359, .364, .365 and .365. His xwOBAs, on the other hand, still show a little decline: .391, .365, .380, .366, .367, .340. Still, it’s been a really impressive season, and getting to 100 runs scored (maybe) and 100 RBI (almost certainly) on the moribund Giants offense is one heck of an accomplishment.
- The Orioles getting swept by Red Sox over the weekend, dropping their postseason odds at Fangraphs to just three percent, would seem to greatly increase the chances that Kyle Bradish gets shut down with a week or two to go. He’s up to 152 innings in his first full year back from Tommy John, and he’s not exactly doing his best work at the moment.
- Kyle Harrison might have lost his rotation spot with his performance Sunday against the Reds, though I thought about keeping him on the list anyway, since he could be well set up for wins in middle relief if moved to the pen. In the end, he didn’t quite make the cut. It will be really interesting to see how the Brewers play things the rest of the way. I imagine both Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson will make a couple of shorter starts in an attempt to save bullets for October.
- It’ll be nice to see Corbin Burnes back on a major league mound Tuesday, but given that he threw just two innings in his lone rehab start after Tommy John, so I couldn’t see including him here just yet. San Diego’s Nick Pivetta, on the other hand, at least made it up to 4 1/3 innings in his last rehab start as he returns from an elbow injury. That gets him a spot on the bottom of the list, even if he’s a long shot to get a win Monday in his return.

item.content:encoded:
Why Aaron Boone could be in postseason 'hell' with Yankees originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees are looking to end a 17-year World Series drought.
Aaron Boone has completed eight of those years as Yankees manager.
This could be a crucial postseason for Boone's future with the AL East club, but New York's ownership and front office have always shown confidence in the skipper.
If three-time MVP Aaron Judge is unable to play in the postseason due to his calf strain, the Yankees will face a difficult task to end their World Series-less streak.
Elsewhere on the diamond, Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes Boone will have to hit the right buttons with the infield alignment.
"However, Aaron Boone is about to be in second-guessing hell in October as it pertains to when and where to deploy George Lombard Jr., Anthony Volpe, José Caballero, Amed Rosario and Ryan McMahon at shortstop and third base," Miller wrote.
Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. would complicate things further if he returns from the injured list before the playoffs.
Volpe has been playing well at second base, but Chisholm offers a higher offensive ceiling.
Boone could consider moving Volpe or Chisholm to third base to keep both players in the lineup. If so, does Caballero become limited to pinch-running duties?
McMahon is Boone's best defensive third baseman, but he offers little (.208/.275/.343, .618 OPS) with a bat in hand.
It seems likely Lombard will stick at shortstop, but Boone and his coaching staff have to be racking his brain trying to figure out what's best for the team.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Monday Mailbag 9/21: State of the Bullpen, Aaron Judge's World Series Window, and More
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
item.description: The New York Yankees won't win the American League East after dropping two out of three games to the Arizona Diamondbacks and are now looking at another Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. The rest of this season will now be about figuring out their roster heading into October, and this Rays series won't mean much. There are plenty of questions from fans about what the roster should look like in the final week of the season. And if you're curious about that, reach out to Joseph Randazzo
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees won't win the American League East after dropping two out of three games to the Arizona Diamondbacks and are now looking at another Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. The rest of this season will now be about figuring out their roster heading into October, and this Rays series won't mean much.
There are plenty of questions from fans about what the roster should look like in the final week of the season. And if you're curious about that, reach out to Joseph Randazzo on X or Instagram at @YankeeLibrarian. Fans can ask anything, from questions about bullpen trust trees to what to do with Jazz Chisholm Jr. when he's activated.
The state of the bullpen
Who do you trust in the bullpen outside of Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, and David Bednar?@Mattmann1199 on Instagram
At this point, the two best names behind them are Will Warren and John Schreiber. It's likely that they'll be without Ryan Weathers, and that is the name I would have gone with. Now it's probably Schreiber, but I'm not too convinced about this answer.
Since Luis Gil has been blowing 100 out of the bullpen, they can see what they have in him as a pen arm heading into October. None of these answers inspire much, but they have somehow been one of the best bullpens in baseball.
A returning bat
Where should Jazz Chisholm Jr. play when they activate him@theezratakeshita on Instagram
Chisholm should probably go to second base. Volpe has been okay, but since his big debut against the Colorado Rockies, he has gone 7-for-33. He has two doubles, three stolen bases, and two RBI.
Since Boston has a ton of lefty starters, they can probably start a game with Volpe and then go to Chisholm later. That feels like what the Yankees will do, and it's probably the case if Volpe is scorching the ball. Of course, there is still time for Volpe to make things interesting here.
Judge's World Series dreams
The World Series window for Judge is closing. Might he go without ever winning one?@_not_mikeee on Instagram
That is absolutely on the table. There are some great players who have never won a championship. Dan Marino, Barry Bonds, and Henrik Lundqvist never got their ring. Granted, the Scott Hunter character in Heated Rivalry feels like it's loosely based on mid-2010s Lundqvist, but that might only half-count since it's a work of fiction.
A wild storyline would be the Yankees winning a World Series this year without Judge. Imagine the chaos of his legacy talks if that happens.
Job statuses
Is there a scenario that gets Cash or Boone fired this year?@kirby.phillips7 on Instagram
These questions are always easy to answer. Probably not this year. Cashman will probably go out on his own accord. Boone is the most likely candidate to get fired, but there aren't many teams that are going to axe a manager who kept their team afloat and in postseason contention with the amount of injuries they had. When baseball comes back after the lockout, those two will probably still be here.
Missing the playoffs again might do it for them, but the last time that happened, they stayed. It does feel like they have unlimited security in New York.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees playoff roster prediction: Who makes the cut with division dreams dwindling ahead of Rays series?
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: Shortly after getting walked-off by the Diamondbacks on Saturday night, the Yankees acknowledged their reality. “Mathematically, [it’s] probably pretty tough, but you never know,” Cody Bellinger said of winning the American League East. Unable to bounce back with an 8-4 loss in Sunday’s series finale against Arizona, the second-place Yankees are now six games back of the division-leading Rays with seven games left in the regular season. The rivals will play four of those games against each other
item.content:encoded:
Shortly after getting walked-off by the Diamondbacks on Saturday night, the Yankees acknowledged their reality.
“Mathematically, [it’s] probably pretty tough, but you never know,” Cody Bellinger said of winning the American League East.
Unable to bounce back with an 8-4 loss in Sunday’s series finale against Arizona, the second-place Yankees are now six games back of the division-leading Rays with seven games left in the regular season. The rivals will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium this week, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday.
Aaron Boone acknowledged that his team will probably have to sweep the Rays just for a crack at the division crown, as FanGraphs gave the Yankees a measly 2.7% chance of winning the AL East before Sunday’s game.
“There’s still a chance,” Cam Schlittler said, “but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
While the Yankees still technically have a shot to defy the odds, the far likelier scenario is that their postseason begins on Sept. 29 at home against Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year.
With that in mind, let’s try to predict what the club’s roster could look like for that series.
Hitters (15): Ben Rice, Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones, Trent Grisham, Cody Bellinger, Ryan McMahon, George Lombard Jr., Paul Goldschmidt, Luis García Jr., Jazz Chisholm Jr., José Caballero, Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez, Anthony Volpe, Amed Rosario
With the Yankees providing minimal info on Aaron Judge’s calf strain, it can’t be assumed he’ll be available.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. could return from a sprained thumb as soon as Tuesday. Meanwhile, Trent Grisham is still in play as a playoff option as he recovers from a hamstring strain, but Boone said that activating him before the end of the regular season is “complicated,” partly due to roster logistics.
With Max Schuemann presumably the corresponding move for Chisholm, the Yankees would have to option someone else if they activated Grisham before the playoffs. That someone wouldn’t be able to be recalled for 10 days barring a new injury; it seems like Jasson Domínguez is being protected from that window in case he’s needed for the Wild Card roster.
Grisham has been doing baseball activities and is “pretty deep into his running progression,” Boone said. If he is on the Wild Card roster, the Yankees will have an interesting decision to make between him and Spencer Jones in center field.
Third base could also be a conundrum, as Ryan McMahon and José Caballero don’t offer much offensively, and Amed Rosario is a poor defender. He’s only on the roster as an option against lefties, even though he hasn’t been great against them.
Another idea would be to use Volpe, who has been playing second, at third against lefties since he played a few games there in the minors this season. However, he doesn’t have a strong arm, and he hasn’t been working at third base since being recalled. Volpe said that the Yankees have not talked to him about manning the hot corner before the regular season ends.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we’ll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it.”
Volpe can also play second over Chisholm against lefties.
Pitchers (11): Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Clarke Schmidt, John Schreiber, Tim Hill, Ryan Weathers
As things stand, Carlos Rodón, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are scheduled to pitch against the Rays, in that order. That would give Cole, who has struggled to get swing-and-miss, an extra day of rest if he were to start Game 1 of the Wild Card round. Schlittler, the AL Cy Young frontrunner, would be on regular rest if tabbed for Game 1.
Because the Wild Card round is a best-of-three series, Rodón isn’t needed, especially with Will Warren expected to work out of the bullpen and able to provide length.
Warren, slated to make one more start this season after struggling on Sunday, is one of a few converted starters who could impact the Bombers’ bullpen this postseason. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are the others. Schmidt, being cautious in his return from Tommy John surgery, couldn’t come into Sunday’s game due to some bicep cramping, while Weathers isn’t expected to return from a flexor strain before the regular season ends.
Still, neither Boone nor pitching coach Matt Blake ruled out the idea of Weathers’ first game back coming in the playoffs.
“I don’t know if ‘comfortable’ is [the right word],” Blake said, “but it might be the course of action where he’s the best option even though he hasn’t pitched in the last three or four weeks.”
As for the relievers that the Yankees have leaned on all season, David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick headline the group. All have been used heavily, especially Headrick.
The lefty allowed a grand slam to Nolan Arenado and saw his fastball velocity down an average of 1.3 mph during his major league-leading 79th appearance on Sunday, but he insisted that he feels fine physically. Boone also downplayed concerns over Headrick’s ongoing velocity fluctuations, though he did say that he hopes to get him and other relievers “in a good spot” with some rest ahead of the playoffs.
That said, the Yankees still haven’t been eliminated from the AL East race. They’ll keep trying to take the division from the Rays until they are.
“We’re going to show up Tuesday,” Boone said, “and try and kick their butt.”

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Clarke Schmidt to see doctor amid new injury concerns appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees' bid for the AL East crown may be all but lost, as they sit six games behind division-leader Tampa Bay Rays in the standings with seven games remaining in the regular season, but the important thing is that they have secured a spot in the Wild Card round — marking their 27th postseason berth in 34 seasons (they are currently in the middle of a 34-year winning season streak).
The key now for the Yankees is keeping their key players healthy. While the Yankees have been mostly healthy on the pitching side of things, reliever Clarke Schmidt, who returned to big-league action on September 16 after a lengthy layoff, suffered some bicep cramping on Sunday, which then prevented him from suiting up in their 8-4 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
While Bob Nightengale of USA Today reported that Schmidt's inability to show up on the mound was merely precautionary, he will be meeting with a doctor back in New York to ascertain that he's not suffering from any underlying serious injury that could keep him out for an extended period once more.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Schmidt didn't make his 2026 season debut until September after he underwent elbow surgery (internal brace procedure), so at least he's not suffering any setbacks in that regard.
The 30-year-old righty struck out two in 0.2 innings of work in his only appearance of 2026 in a 5-4 loss for the Yankees against the Minnesota Twins.
The Yankees have already been dealt a huge injury blow, with Aaron Judge, who only recently returned to action, suffering a calf strain that sent him back to the injured list. They already have Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham among lineup regulars already on the IL.
While New York has enough depth to make up for the absences of a few players, they would want to enter the postseason as close to full strength as they can get. With the Wild Card round set to begin in nine days, they have some time to get it together from a health standpoint.
Related: Yankees' Spencer Jones shuts down injury concern ahead of postseason

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could activate Jazz Chisholm Jr. as soon as Tuesday, raising questions about Anthony Volpe's role.
Nothing is set yet, manager Aaron Boone said Sunday, according to New York Daily News reporter Gary Phillips. The update came before the Yankees played the Arizona Diamondbacks in Phoenix.
Chisholm sprained his right thumb Sept. 8. The Yankees recalled Volpe, 25, from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre on Sept. 10. They had optioned him in early August after promoting shortstop George Lombard Jr.
Volpe has played second base since then and has produced remarkable numbers.
Through Saturday, he has gone 9-for-31 in nine games since his recall. That is a .290 average with a .333 on-base percentage, a .452 slugging percentage and a .785 OPS.
He has one home run, two doubles, seven RBIs and four runs scored. Volpe has walked twice, struck out four times and stolen four bases without being caught.
Anthony Volpe's Future Is Still Not Known
Volpe could also see time at third base in the coming days. Boone fielded a question about using Volpe there, Phillips reported.
"We'll see," Boone said. "First things first, getting Jazz back and then we'll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it."
Volpe also addressed the idea, Phillips reported.
He said the Yankees have not talked to him about playing third base before the regular season ends. He said he felt comfortable there the few times he played third base in the minors.
At Triple-A, Volpe made 19 starts at second base, 15 at shortstop and three at third base.
Chisholm is batting .232 with 19 home runs and 40 stolen bases in 134 games this season.
The Yankees open their final homestand Tuesday with a doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays. They entered Sunday at 89-65.
Trent Grisham is Out for the Regular Season
Boone said the Yankees do not expect to activate Trent Grisham before the regular season ends, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reported.
Grisham could still be on the playoff roster, Boone said.
The New York Post's Greg Joyce reported that roster complications are part of the reason. The Yankees would have to send a player down and could not recall him for 10 days, Joyce reported.
Joyce contrasted that with activating Grisham directly onto the playoff roster.
Grisham has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 5 with a Grade 2 right hamstring strain. He left a Sept. 4 game against the San Diego Padres in the third inning. It is his second right hamstring strain of the season.
Grisham is batting .211 with 18 home runs and 59 RBIs this season. The 29-year-old will be a free agent after the season.

Aunque se trata de un duro golpe para los Yankees, Judg
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge fue retirado del enfrentamiento de los Yankees contra los Twins el miércoles durante la sexta entrada. Estaba por tomar su tercer turno al bat del juego cuando fue sustituido por Heliot Ramos. El viernes, fue colocado oficialmente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, lo que lo mantendrá fuera hasta el final de la temporada regular y posiblemente durante parte de la postemporada.
Aunque se trata de un duro golpe para los Yankees, Judge está lejos de ser el único jugador destacado que enfrenta una lesión de cara a la postemporada. Echemos un vistazo a la situación actual en la lista de lesionados de cada equipo contendiente mientras se acerca la postemporada, destacando a algunos jugadores importantes que actualmente están fuera y ofreciendo la información más reciente sobre cuándo se espera que regresen, si es que lo hacen.
Te puede interesar: Evaluando a los Yankees sin Aaron Judge y la extraña caída de Kyle Tucker
Braves
Reynaldo Lopez, SP
Lopez tuvo problemas contra los Cubs el lunes y fue retirado del juego después de tres entradas; posteriormente fue colocado en la lista de lesionados debido a molestias en el hombro derecho, una dolencia que, según reportes, ha sufrido durante toda la temporada. Lopez se perdió prácticamente toda la temporada de 2025 debido a una lesión en el hombro y, a pesar de las molestias persistentes derivadas de ese problema, lanzó en 26 juegos este año, incluidas 13 aperturas, y registra una ERA de 4.54. El equipo no ha dado ninguna indicación sobre su estado para la postemporada, pero no parece probable que esté disponible para lanzar en octubre, lo que reduciría aún más las opciones de Atlanta en su rotación abridora.
Bryce Elder, SP
Elder fue colocado en la lista de lesionados el 9 de septiembre y se sometió a una cirugía artroscópica de rodilla, aunque se espera que solo se pierda entre tres y cuatro semanas de acción. Había estado lidiando con molestias en la rodilla desde el All-Star break y podría estar en condiciones de regresar en octubre, aunque Atlanta podría necesitar avanzar profundamente en la postemporada para que Elder alcance a regresar.
Phillies
Jesus Luzardo, SP
Luzardo fue colocado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días el martes debido a una inflamación en el hombro. Será elegible para ser activado el 27 de septiembre, el último día de la temporada regular. Está por verse si estará listo para regresar en ese momento, pero el equipo confía en contar con el pitcher zurdo All-Star en la postemporada. Después de ser colocado en la lista de lesionados, Luzardo dijo a los reporteros que el plan es que pueda lanzar en octubre.
Brad Keller, RP
Keller estará fuera hasta 2027 después de sufrir un desgarro del UCL en el codo de lanzar, dejando fuera por el resto de la temporada a uno de los relevistas importantes de los Phillies. En 32 apariciones esta temporada, Keller registró una ERA de 4.02, con 32 strikeouts, 13 bases por bolas y tres salvamentos en 31 1/3 entradas.
Brewers
Brandon Woodruff, SP
Woodruff está fuera desde el 5 de julio, pero todavía existe una pequeña posibilidad de que pueda regresar en la parte final de la temporada. Woodruff está lidiando con una lesión en la cápsula del hombro derecho, aunque tuvo un buen desempeño durante la primera mitad de la campaña. En nueve aperturas, el pitcher de 33 años registró una ERA de 2.98, con 47 strikeouts y apenas 10 bases por bolas en 45 1/3 entradas. No está claro qué papel podría asumir para Milwaukee en la postemporada después de perderse casi tres meses completos, aunque podría aportar entradas valiosas desde el bullpen si el equipo considera que todavía no está listo para asumir la carga de trabajo de un abridor.
Cubs
Justin Steele, SP
Steele no ha lanzado en MLB desde abril del año pasado, después de atravesar una larga ausencia debido a una lesión en el codo del brazo con el que lanza. Actualmente se encuentra en rehabilitación en Triple A, pero el equipo pretende que haga algunas apariciones más antes de potencialmente activarlo de cara a la postemporada, tomando en cuenta cuánto tiempo ha pasado desde que lanzó en un juego de MLB. El manager Craig Counsell dijo que el equipo está “contento con lo que está sucediendo. Pero [Steele] va a necesitar lanzar más”, antes de regresar.
Ben Brown, SP
La temporada de Brown terminó después de sufrir una lesión en el cuello y experimentar un retroceso en su recuperación tras una sesión de lanzamientos en el complejo de spring training del equipo en Arizona a finales de agosto. No podrá regresar para la postemporada y, en cambio, se concentrará en estar listo para la campaña de 2027.
Dodgers
Shohei Ohtani, SP/DH
Ohtani ha estado lidiando con lesiones en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho y fue colocado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días. No ha lanzado desde el 3 de julio debido al estrés que soporta su rodilla lesionada cuando lanza desde el montículo. Será elegible para regresar de la lista de lesionados el 23 de septiembre, y el manager Dave Roberts ha indicado que espera que Ohtani vuelva a jugar antes de que concluya la temporada regular. Ohtani dijo que se concentrará en batear cuando regrese a la acción y que probablemente no volverá a lanzar en 2026.
Dalton Rushing, C
El catcher suplente de los Dodgers tuvo mucha actividad detrás del plato durante la prolongada ausencia de Will Smith, pero fue colocado en la lista de lesionados el 6 de septiembre debido a molestias en el codo derecho, derivadas de un desgarro parcial del UCL. El equipo ha dicho que Rushing no volverá a desempeñarse como catcher esta temporada, pero mantiene la esperanza de que pueda contribuir como bateador designado o bateador emergente durante la postemporada.
Edwin Diaz, RP
Las lesiones han obstaculizado la primera temporada de Diaz con los Dodgers, y volvió a la lista de lesionados a mediados de agosto después de una mala racha de actuaciones. Se espera que el pitcher de 32 años regrese el viernes, aunque parece que el equipo todavía no ha decidido si siquiera estará en el roster de postemporada, tomando en cuenta sus problemas durante el año. Diaz registra una poco atractiva ERA de 11.85 esta temporada, con siete salvamentos y 19 strikeouts en 13 2/3 entradas. Si Diaz no logra mostrar cierto nivel de estabilidad sobre el montículo durante el tramo final, podría no estar en los planes del equipo para octubre.
Andy Pages, CF
Pages está en la lista de lesionados desde el 22 de agosto debido a una fractura en la mano izquierda, pero se espera que regrese antes del final de la temporada regular y probablemente no necesite una asignación de rehabilitación. Pages estaba teniendo el mejor año de su carrera antes de la lesión, con 21 home runs, 80 carreras impulsadas y un OPS de .797. Si regresa a la acción sin contratiempos, Pages debería estar listo para la postemporada y recuperar su puesto como center fielder titular de Los Angeles.
Roki Sasaki, SP/RP
Una ampolla en el dedo medio de la mano derecha llevó a Sasaki a la lista de lesionados a finales de agosto, pero se acerca a su regreso después de realizar el miércoles una sesión de bullpen con bateadores. Estará disponible para la postemporada, pero todavía no se ha determinado qué papel tendrá. Jack Harris, de California Post, reporta que es probable que Sasaki lance desde el bullpen en octubre, aunque podría ser utilizado en la rotación en caso de que se presente una lesión de un pitcher hacia el final de la temporada.
Blake Snell, SP
Snell abandonó su apertura del miércoles debido a un problema en la ingle, pero no está claro si necesitará pasar por la lista de lesionados como consecuencia. Snell hizo su debut de temporada el 9 de mayo, pero fue colocado en la lista de lesionados debido a una lesión en el codo. No regresó sino hasta el 11 de agosto, después de lo cual realizó seis aperturas antes de que surgiera el problema en la ingle durante su más reciente salida. No está claro si volverá al montículo durante la temporada regular, ya que los Dodgers probablemente priorizarán mantenerlo saludable para la postemporada.
Padres
Gavin Sheets, DH
Sheets está fuera de acción desde finales de agosto mientras lidia con un esguince en el pie, pero retomó el swing a mediados de septiembre y podría estar listo para regresar en la postemporada. La expectativa, de acuerdo con AJ Cassavell, de MLB.com, es que Sheets regrese como bateador designado o bateador emergente y no juegue a la defensiva en octubre.
Joe Musgrove, SP
Musgrove no ha realizado una apertura desde 2024, debido a que atraviesa una larga recuperación de una cirugía Tommy John. Mientras intentaba aumentar gradualmente su carga de trabajo durante su rehabilitación en las Ligas Menores, Musgrove ha experimentado problemas durante la recuperación de su brazo operado. Todavía es posible que regrese antes del final de la temporada, aunque en esta etapa parece más probable que tenga un papel desde el bullpen.
Rays
Shane McClanahan, SP
McClanahan fue colocado en la lista de lesionados el 4 de septiembre después de abandonar su apertura debido a rigidez en el antebrazo. McClanahan dijo en ese momento que no creía que la lesión fuera demasiado seria, pero los Rays decidieron ser cautelosos con su pitcher estrella. La expectativa es que McClanahan esté listo para volver a lanzar antes del final de la temporada, por lo que debería estar disponible en octubre si no sufre un retroceso.
Tyler Wells, RP
Wells también fue colocado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a rigidez en el antebrazo izquierdo el 15 de septiembre, y se espera que necesite permanecer el tiempo mínimo fuera antes de regresar para la postemporada. Ha sido una pieza importante del bullpen de los Rays desde que llegó en un intercambio con los Orioles, por lo que contar nuevamente con él en octubre será importante para Tampa.
Yankees
Aaron Judge, RF
Judge fue retirado del juego del miércoles contra los Twins debido a lo que el equipo describió como rigidez en la parte baja de la pierna. Se pudo ver al bateador haciendo una mueca de dolor después de un swing sin contacto durante el juego y fue retirado antes de su tercer turno al bat. El viernes, los Yankees lo colocaron oficialmente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha. Esto lo mantendrá fuera hasta el final de la temporada regular y posiblemente durante parte de la postemporada. Judge se perdió 84 juegos esta temporada mientras lidiaba con una lesión en las costillas, pero esta es una dolencia completamente diferente. Los aficionados en Nueva York estarán conteniendo la respiración mientras esperan una actualización más detallada sobre el estado del tres veces MVP, pero se trata de una gran preocupación para el equipo con la postemporada a poco más de una semana de distancia.
Giancarlo Stanton, DH
Stanton continúa fuera después de lesionarse la pantorrilla a principios de esta temporada y posteriormente sufrir una dolencia en la otra pantorrilla mientras se recuperaba. Stanton todavía no ha sido descartado para el resto de la temporada, aunque el equipo no ha proporcionado mucha información sobre su estado. El slugger, propenso a las lesiones, solo ha disputado 24 juegos esta temporada y no juega desde finales de abril, por lo que su disponibilidad para la postemporada continúa en duda.
Trent Grisham, CF
Grisham sufrió una distensión de Grado 2 en el tendón de la corva derecho y está en la lista de lesionados desde el 5 de septiembre. El equipo no espera que el outfielder regrese antes del final de la temporada regular, pero todavía no se ha definido su disponibilidad para la postemporada. Grisham disputó 121 juegos este año y registró 18 home runs y 59 carreras impulsadas, con un OPS de .703.
Fernando Cruz, RP
El relevista de los Yankees fue diagnosticado con un desgarro parcial del UCL en el codo derecho. Aunque no se ha recomendado una cirugía, Cruz todavía no ha reanudado sus lanzamientos, por lo que su disponibilidad para la postemporada está en duda. El veterano registra una ERA de 3.13, con 67 strikeouts en 54 2/3 entradas esta temporada, además de dos salvamentos.
Jazz Chisholm Jr., 2B
Chisholm está en la lista de lesionados desde el 10 de septiembre después de sufrir un esguince en el pulgar, pero se espera que regrese a la acción antes del final de la temporada regular. Chisholm dijo a los reporteros que tiene como objetivo regresar el 22 de septiembre, antes de que los Yankees comiencen una serie final como locales contra los Rays y Orioles. Esta temporada, Chisholm ha estado aproximadamente en el promedio de la liga a la ofensiva, mientras registra un porcentaje de slugging de .403, el más bajo de su carrera, con 19 home runs, pero ha robado 40 bases, igualando la cifra más alta de su carrera.
Red Sox
Garrett Crochet, SP
Crochet ha estado fuera durante la mayor parte del año debido a una lesión en el hombro izquierdo, pero el equipo todavía tiene la esperanza de que pueda regresar para la postemporada. Crochet realizó el martes una sesión de bullpen de 30 lanzamientos y existe la posibilidad de que haga una aparición durante la temporada regular para prepararse para los playoffs. Cuando regrese con Boston, sin embargo, se espera que sea utilizado desde el bullpen, ya que no tendrá suficiente tiempo para aumentar gradualmente su carga de trabajo como abridor.
Ceddanne Rafaela, CF
Rafaela sufrió una distensión en el cuádriceps durante la primera semana de septiembre, pero parece estar cerca de regresar a la acción antes del final de la temporada regular. Rafaela bateó el jueves contra una máquina Trajekt y podría participar en un juego de rehabilitación con Triple A Worcester durante el fin de semana antes de reincorporarse a los Red Sox durante la última serie como locales del equipo.
Tanner Houck, RP
Houck no ha lanzado desde mayo de 2025, pero se acerca a su regreso después de la larga recuperación que implica una cirugía Tommy John. Realizó una aparición de rehabilitación con Triple A Worcester el martes y cada vez está más cerca de regresar a las Mayores. Cuando vuelva a los Red Sox, al igual que Crochet, se espera que lance desde el bullpen durante la postemporada.
Guardians
Rhys Hoskins, 1B/DH
Hoskins fue colocado en la lista de lesionados de 10 días el 19 de agosto debido a una inflamación en la parte baja de la espalda, pero desde entonces recibió autorización para comenzar una progresión de bateo mientras avanza en su recuperación. El equipo espera que Hoskins esté listo para octubre, aunque no está claro si será activado de la lista de lesionados antes del final de la temporada regular.
Astros
Carlos Correa, IF
Correa no regresará esta temporada después de decidir esta semana que se concentrará en recuperarse para 2027. El shortstop está fuera desde mayo, cuando se sometió a una cirugía en el tobillo izquierdo. Existía cierta esperanza de que pudiera regresar a finales de esta temporada, pero parece que no asumirá el riesgo y, en cambio, se concentrará en el próximo año.
Rangers
Joc Pederson, DH
Pederson recibió un pelotazo en la mano durante el enfrentamiento del 12 de septiembre contra los Diamondbacks, aunque está intentando jugar pese a la lesión con los Rangers en plena pelea por el título de la AL West. Recibirá tratamiento mientras busca combatir la inflamación en la mano y probablemente solo estará en el lineup contra pitchers derechos.
Publicado originalmente en www.sportsillustrated.com el 18/09/2026, traducido al español para SI México.

item.dc:creator: John Griffin
item.description: It’s Sunday once more, and you know what that means — it’s time for our weekly social media roundup! This weekend has been yet another veritable whirlwind in the Bronx, as the team celebrated a postseason appearance, bid farewell to a fan favorite, closed an era of minor league baseball, and watched as their Captain hit the shelf once more. item.content:encoded:
It’s Sunday once more, and you know what that means — it’s time for our weekly social media roundup! This weekend has been yet another veritable whirlwind in the Bronx, as the team celebrated a postseason appearance, bid farewell to a fan favorite, closed an era of minor league baseball, and watched as their Captain hit the shelf once more. With so much in store, let’s get started!
Another Celebration in Minnesota
It was deja vu all over again! For what feels like the fifty millionth time, the Yankees celebrated in Minnesota, as they clinched a postseason berth earlier this week with a victory over their favorite AL Central punching bag.
The Roberto Clemente Award
This week, the New York Yankees named Carlos Rodón their nominee for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award. The team honored the Rodón Foundation, which sets out to help families suffering with fertility issues.
In Service
Yankees reliever Brent Headrick welcomed Henry Ledlowe from his hometown in Illinois to the Bronx, courtesy of the National Down Syndrome Society. Unfortunately, the Instagram post cannot be embedded, but can be found here.
The Jazz Chisholm Jr. Foundation, meanwhile, marked the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
Where’s Oswaldo? Unfortunately, Cincy.
This week, the Yankees designated fan favorite Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment in order to make room on the 40-man roster for Clarke Schmidt. Unfortunately, he was claimed off waivers by the Cincinnati Reds, and while we’re all excited to see him (hopefully) get some regular playing time — as he was very much blocked in the Bronx — it will be sad to see the human golden retriever, well-loved by the fans and players alike, in a different uniform.
A testament to his popularity is the fact that the Yankees, RailRiders, Patriots, and YES Network all posted farewells to him on their social media accounts. David Cone also came back to Twitter briefly in order to wish him well.
Farewell to the RailRiders
Starting next year, the Yankees’ Triple-A affiliate will undergo its second rebrand since joining the Yankees family, abandoning the RailRider moniker in exchange for a new nickname which has yet to be revealed. To honor the end of the era, Clint Frazier — who self-identifies as a Scranton RailRider more than anyone else in baseball — threw out the ceremonial first pitch prior to their final game.
Road Trip Nonsense
Meredith Marakovitz, Suzyn Waldman, and Dave Simms always have fun on the road trips, and this one is no different!
The Knicks are Back
This week, the Yankees will be hosting Josh Hart bobblehead night, celebrating the 2026 NBA Champion (and 2016 NCAA Champion!) who is related to Yankees legend Elston Howard. Fun fact — this has been scheduled since last year, so it actually predates the Knicks’ championship; what fantastic luck for the marketing team!
Celebrating Howie
Last Sunday, Mets broadcaster Howie Rose called his last game at Yankee Stadium. The Yankees set out to make the day special, and many of his friends and coworkers in the Yankees broadcast teams celebrated his career with him.
Official Videos
First, the latest episode of Behind the NY gives us a behind-the scenes look at the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
Then, we got a behind-the-scenes look of David Bednar entering the game on Sunday.
Last, but not least, we have Cody Bellinger talking about his story.
We’ve got a special edition of this week’s Question of the Day, as we not only have the Yankees answering questions, we’ve got the Somerset Patriots reading Thank You Cards as they wrap up their season.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are in the middle of a three-game series against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix.
The Yankees won the first game of the series 9-2 on Friday. The Diamondbacks bounced back with a 5-2 win on Saturday. The finale is slated to begin at 4:10 p.m. EDT on Sunday.
Before Sunday's game, the Yankees announced updates on Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham.
New York Yankees Announce Jazz Chisholm Jr., Trent Grisham News Before Diamondbacks Game
The New York Daily News' Gary Phillips wrote on X: Nothing set yet, but Jazz Chisholm Jr. could be activated as soon as Tuesday, Aaron Boone said.
: Trent Grisham is unlikely to be activated before the regular season ends, in part because of roster complications — Yankees would have to send someone down and not be able to call them back up for 10 days vs. possibility of activating Grisham right onto playoff roster.
Trent Grisham is unlikely to be activated before the regular season ends, in part because of roster complications — Yankees would have to send someone down and not be able to call them back up for 10 days vs. possibility of activating Grisham right onto playoff roster.
— Greg Joyce (@GJoyce9) September 20, 2026
Looking at Jazz Chisholm Jr.
Chisholm has been on the injured list with a right thumb strain since Sept. 10.
This season, Chisholm has hit .232/.312/.403 with 19 home runs and 55 RBI over 134 games. He is set to be a free agent at the end of the season.
Looking at Trent Grisham
Grisham has been on the injured list with a right hamstring strain since Sept. 5.
This season, Grisham has hit .211/.308/.395 with 18 home runs and 59 RBI over 121 games. He is set to be a free agent at the end of the season.
New York Yankees Right Now
The Yankees have already clinched a postseason berth. They hold a 5 1/2 game lead over the Boston Red Sox for the top AL Wild Card spot with an 89-65 record.
Meanwhile, New York is five games behind the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the American League East.
After the Diamondbacks series, the Yankees will host the Rays for a four-game set and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games to finish the regular season.
