item.title: [bolavip.com] NY Yankees, Aaron Boone hope to have Trent Grisham for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Matías Persuh
item.description: The New York Yankees are one of the teams that will compete in the 2026 MLB playoffs, and they are looking to have as many players as possible at full strength. According to insider Bryan Hoch on X, Aaron Boone said that Trent Grisham isn’t expected to be activated before the end of the regular season, but the Yanks hope to have him on their playoff roster. The manager also provided an update on other injured players. Jazz Chisholm Jr. is “in play, potentially” to be activated on Tuesday, and th
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are one of the teams that will compete in the 2026 MLB playoffs, and they are looking to have as many players as possible at full strength. According to insider Bryan Hoch on X, Aaron Boone said that Trent Grisham isn’t expected to be activated before the end of the regular season, but the Yanks hope to have him on their playoff roster.
The manager also provided an update on other injured players. Jazz Chisholm Jr. is “in play, potentially” to be activated on Tuesday, and the Pinstripes are also hopeful of having him back for the Wild Card round.
With little time remaining in the regular season, it would seem wise for the Bronx Bombers not to rush any player back. On the other hand, having already clinched a playoff spot could be beneficial for giving Grisham some playing time on the field.
What happened to Trent Grisham?
Trent Grisham is back on the shelf after tweaking his right hamstring again during a stolen base attempt against San Diego on September 4th. The Yankees officially placed him on the 10-day injured list on September 5th with a moderate Grade 2 strain, making this his second IL stint for the same hamstring issue this season after missing roughly three weeks back in June and July.
Xander Bogaerts #2 of the San Diego Padres tags out Trent Grisham #12 of the New York Yankees.
He’s been sidelined since then, putting his status up in the air as the regular season winds down and leaving the Yanks hoping he can heal up in time to be a factor in the postseason.
The Yankees’ final stretch
Aaron Boone and the Yankees are heading into the final stretch of the regular season, closing things out with a huge six-game homestand at the Stadium against two division foes: three against the Tampa Bay Rays followed by three with the Baltimore Orioles.
They’re coming off a long road swing that had a bit of everything—sweeping a short two-game set against the Minnesota Twins, but dropping two out of three in Phoenix against the Arizona Diamondbacks. Having already clinched their playoff ticket, these final home games are all about locking up seeding, dialing in the bullpen, and sharpening the bats before the October pressure cooker begins.

The dynamic 28-year-old infielder has been sidelined since September 9 due to a right thumb sprain but has made significant progress in his recovery over the past few days. It sounds like he should be ready to go early in the week, which will cut into the playing time of Anthony Volpe who has been seeing regular action at second base.
item.content:encoded:
Yankees’ manager Aaron Boone suggested that Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb) could be activated from the injured list as early as Tuesday.

The dynamic 28-year-old infielder has been sidelined since September 9 due to a right thumb sprain but has made significant progress in his recovery over the past few days. It sounds like he should be ready to go early in the week, which will cut into the playing time of Anthony Volpe who has been seeing regular action at second base.

item.title: [MLB.com] ¿Qué les espera a los Yankees sin Judge en esta última semana?
item.dc:creator: David Venn

item.content:encoded:
Nueva York llegó al domingo a 5.0 juegos de la cima del Este de la Liga Americana, detrás de los encendidos Rays. Tampa Bay estuvo programado para concluir su serie en casa ante los Medias Rojas el domingo, al mismo tiempo que los Yankees se preparaban para hacer lo propio frente a los Diamondbacks en Arizona.
Luego, los Bombarderos del Bronx recibirán desde el martes al equipo de St. Petersburg en el Bronx para una crucial serie de cuatro juegos. Dicha serie podría apretar la lucha por el Este, o de una vez por todas ser decisiva para que los Rays terminen de ganar la llave y dejar a los Yankees como un Comodín. Después de eso, Nueva York concluirá su temporada regular con una serie de tres choques en casa frente a Baltimore.
Ahora, la gran interrogante para Nueva York es cómo jugará el equipo sin Judge en la alineación.
“Tengo confianza”, dijo el dirigente del equipo, Aaron Boone. “Obvio, quitar al mejor jugador lo hace más difícil. Pero creo que en las últimas semanas, hemos empezado a encontrar el ritmo un poco a nivel ofensivo”.
Es cierto. Aunque los Yankees llegaron al domingo en el lugar número 21 de Grandes Ligas en carreras anotadas después del Juego de Estrellas, en los últimos 30 días, han anotado la mayor cantidad de carreras en la Liga Americana, superados sólo por los fuertes equipos de Cerveceros y Cachorros en las Mayores. Y en ese trecho, están empatados en la cima del Joven Circuito con 37 jonrones… incluyendo uno solo de Judge, quien dio uno el lunes en Minnesota como parte de su trecho de siete partidos jugados entre su fractura en una costura sufrida al principio de la campaña y su lesión de ahora, un tirón en la pantorrilla derecha.
“Sabemos que somos capaces de ganar juegos”, expresó Boone. “Hemos tenido que jugar sin muchas piezas cruciales en diferentes momentos y durante largos trechos de la temporada, así que nuestra expectativa es salir y ganar. Y se acabó el tema”.
Otra declaración acertada. Dirigiendo un equipo que ha contado con apenas 24 juegos de Giancarlo Stanton, los Yankees – como la gran mayoría de los conjuntos – han sabido soportar lesiones de otras piezas clave. En estos momentos, esperan la llegada muy pronto de figuras como Jazz Chisholm Jr., Trent Grisham y posiblemente Ryan Weathers.
“Espero que más y más piezas puedan volver y hacer de este equipo uno más formidable el resto del camino”, dijo Boone.
Por supuesto, el punto fuerte de los Yankees del 2026 ha sido su pitcheo. Encabezados por el candidato al Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, Cam Schlittler, los Yankees son los líderes en MLB con efectividad colectiva de 3.18, 0.38 mejor que el segundo mejor equipo en ese sentido, los Cerveceros. Su rotación abridora es la mejor del béisbol, con promedio de carreras limpias de 3.25, a la vez que su bullpen está empatado con el de Boston en el primer puesto con 3.09.
Entonces, aunque la presencia de Judge representaría una gran mejoría para cualquier lineup del planeta, los Yankees han sabido sobrevivir sin él en sentido general desde el 31 de mayo. ¿Será ése el caso en una posible Serie de Comodín frente a los Medias Rojas la próxima semana si no vuelve “El Juez”?
“Espero que más y más piezas puedan volver y hacer de este equipo uno más formidable el resto del camino”, dijo Boone, sin mencionar específicamente a Judge en ese contexto.
Por supuesto, el punto fuerte de los Yankees del 2026 ha sido su pitcheo. Encabezados por el candidato al Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, Cam Schlittler, los Yankees son los líderes en MLB con efectividad colectiva de 3.18, 0.38 mejor que el segundo mejor equipo en ese sentido, los Cerveceros. Su rotación abridora es la mejor del béisbol, con promedio de carreras limpias de 3.25, a la vez que su bullpen está empatado con el de Boston en el primer puesto con 3.09.
Entonces, aunque la presencia de Judge representaría una gran mejoría para cualquier lineup del planeta, los Yankees han sabido sobrevivir sin él en sentido general desde el 31 de mayo. ¿Será ése el caso en una posible Serie de Comodín frente a los Medias Rojas la próxima semana si no vuelve “El Juez”?
Es una pregunta que nadie en el universo de los Yankees quiere ponderar en este momento.
“Esperamos tener el mejor resultado, pero todo depende de cómo irá el proceso de sanación”, manifestó Boone.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] La Novia De Anthony Volpe Vuelve A Ser Noticia En Arizona Mientras La Estrella De Los Yankees Se Enfrenta A Los Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Inna Zeyger
item.description: PHOENIX — Anthony Volpe tiene muchas cosas en las que centrarse ahora que los Yankees se preparan para octubre. Su novia, Elle Jowett, por su parte, ha encontrado un rincón mucho más tranquilo de Arizona. Jowett volvió a ser tema de conversación fuera del campo entre los Yankees el domingo, después de compartir unas fotos de una excursión por el sendero Cathedral Rock Trail, en Sedona, mientras Volpe y el equipo de Nueva York estaban en el estado para disputar su serie de tres partidos contra lo
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Anthony Volpe tiene muchas cosas en las que centrarse ahora que los Yankees se preparan para octubre. Su novia, Elle Jowett, por su parte, ha encontrado un rincón mucho más tranquilo de Arizona.
Jowett volvió a ser tema de conversación fuera del campo entre los Yankees el domingo, después de compartir unas fotos de una excursión por el sendero Cathedral Rock Trail, en Sedona, mientras Volpe y el equipo de Nueva York estaban en el estado para disputar su serie de tres partidos contra los Diamondbacks de Arizona.
La modelo, afincada en Nueva York, se fue de excursión a Cathedral Rock y compartió unas fotos en las que aparece meditando en el sendero. Jowett llevaba una camiseta deportiva y unos leggings mientras posaba con el característico paisaje de rocas rojas y el entorno desértico de Sedona de fondo.
El momento hace que una publicación sobre un estilo de vida que, por lo demás, sería muy sencilla, adquiera un toque relacionado con los Yankees.
Mientras Jowett disfrutaba del paisaje de Arizona, Volpe seguía inmerso en una aventura de septiembre muy diferente, a unos 190 kilómetros de distancia, en Phoenix.
Jowett sale a la luz durante una racha importante de los Yankees
Los Yankees ya se han asegurado su participación en el béisbol de octubre, tras conseguir su tercera clasificación consecutiva para la postemporada. Lo que aún está por decidir es su recorrido en la postemporada.
El sábado nos volvió a recordar que los partidos que quedan no son para tomárselos a la ligera.
Arizona venció a Nueva York por 5-3 gracias a un jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith en la novena entrada que dio la victoria a su equipo. Con esta derrota, los Yankees quedan con un balance de 89-65, lo que les mantiene bajo presión en la recta final de la temporada regular.
Volpe participó de lleno en el ataque de Nueva York.
Jugó como segunda base, conectó 1 de 4, bateó un sencillo en la quinta entrada y luego anotó la primera carrera de los Yankees gracias a un fly de sacrificio de Ben Rice.
Esto convierte a la serie en otra buena prueba de fuego de octubre para un equipo de los Yankees que ya tiene asegurada su participación más allá de la temporada regular.
El papel de Volpe en los Yankees ha cambiado radicalmente
El puesto de Volpe en la alineación se ha convertido en uno de los temas más interesantes que rodean al equipo.
Los Yankees lo bajaron a la Triple A durante la segunda mitad de la temporada tras sus problemas ofensivos. Durante su etapa en las ligas menores, Volpe empezó a jugar de segunda base, alejándose de la posición de campocorto que definió sus primeros años en las Grandes Ligas.
Más tarde, Nueva York lo volvió a llamar después de que la lesión en el pulgar de Jazz Chisholm Jr. dejara un hueco en el cuadro.
Volpe anunció su regreso a lo grande el 10 de septiembre, con una actuación de tres hits y cinco carreras impulsadas, que incluyó un grand slam en la victoria de los Yankees por 10-3 sobre Colorado. Después admitió que nada de lo relacionado con su regreso estaba garantizado cuando Nueva York lo envió inicialmente a la Triple A.
Volpe está aprovechando al máximo su segunda oportunidad con los Yankees
Y lo que es más importante para los Yankees, Volpe no ha dejado que ese memorable partido de regreso sea un caso aislado.
En sus últimos ocho partidos hasta el domingo, este jugador de 25 años tenía un promedio de bateo de .296, con un porcentaje de embasado de .345 y un porcentaje de slugging de .481, lo que le da un OPS de .826. Consiguió ocho hits en 27 turnos al bate durante ese periodo, incluyendo dos dobles y un jonrón, además de impulsar siete carreras.
Esas cifras suponen una respuesta significativa por parte de un jugador cuyo futuro en los Yankees parecía mucho menos seguro cuando el club lo envió de vuelta a la Triple A.
El regreso de Volpe también vino acompañado de un cambio de posición. En lugar de recuperar inmediatamente el puesto de campocorto, ha estado jugando en segunda base mientras los Yankees evalúan cómo podría encajar su cuadro interior en octubre.
Este experimento ha añadido otra dimensión a su resurgimiento de final de temporada.
No consiguió ningún hit en sus cuatro turnos al bate durante la victoria del viernes por 9-2 contra Arizona, pero el sábado respondió con un sencillo y una carrera anotada.
La tendencia general sigue siendo alentadora.
Volpe llegó a esta recta final con la necesidad de demostrar que su paso por la Triple A había dado frutos tangibles. En lugar de volver simplemente porque una lesión le había dejado un hueco, ha empezado a dar a los Yankees motivos para seguir dándole oportunidades al bate.
Eso podría ser muy importante cuando el entrenador Aaron Boone empiece a decidir qué combinación de infield le da a Nueva York su mejor alineación para la postemporada.
Elle Jowett ha ido acaparando cada vez más la atención de los Yankees
La aparición de Jowett en Arizona no es la primera vez que su actividad en las redes sociales llama la atención en un momento importante de la temporada de Volpe.
Ella y Volpe se hicieron públicos como pareja durante la temporada de 2025 tras aparecer juntos en la gala Willow Grant de la Fundación Carlos Rodón en Greenwich, Connecticut.
Posteriormente, Jowett asistió a partidos de la postemporada de los Yankees, aunque la pareja ha mantenido en general su relación al margen de sus propias redes sociales.
A principios de este año, Jowett volvió a aparecer en los titulares tras compartir fotos de Los Ángeles más o menos cuando los Yankees enviaron a Volpe a la Triple A. Otros miembros de la gran familia de los Yankees interactuaron con esa publicación.
Más tarde, llamó la atención con otra publicación de modelaje coincidiendo con el regreso de Volpe a las Grandes Ligas.
Ahora, Arizona es el último punto de encuentro entre los mundos separados de la pareja.
El fin de semana de Jowett ha girado en torno a la meditación y al paisaje de rocas rojas de Sedona. El de Volpe, por su parte, ha estado marcado por un equipo de los Yankees , que se dirige a la postemporada, que ha tenido que lidiar con una derrota en la última entrada, un panorama cambiante en el cuadro y decisiones cada vez más importantes sobre su alineación para octubre.
Los contextos no podrían ser más diferentes.
Pero ahora que octubre está a la vuelta de la esquina, ambas han vuelto a poner la vida fuera del campo de Volpe al mismo nivel que uno de los tramos más decisivos de su temporada con los Yankees.
¿Qué le parece? Deje su comentario a continuación.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] What the Yankees' Lineup Should Look Like Without Aaron Judge In October
item.dc:creator: Michael Zeno; Unknown
item.description: Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be. A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be. A scenario is now potentially unfo
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be.
A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be.
A scenario is now potentially unfolding that would have only appeared in Boone's nightmares: a postseason without the best hitter in baseball, with a lineup that struggled mightily without him. Even if they seemed to gradually improve as time went on, particularly in August, it would be a massive blow if he cannot return.
You can't replace a guy like Judge midseason; you can merely do your best to make up for his absence. Fortunately, on a platoon-heavy team like this, they should have plenty of options to build a lineup without him for the playoffs.
What the playoff lineup should look like against right-handed pitching
- Ben Rice (DH)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Luis García Jr. (1B)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Austin Wells (C)
- Ryan McMahon (3B)
This lineup simultaneously features the easiest decisions, but also the roughest circumstances. Having a guy like Judge as the ultimate lineup balancer who mashed both lefties and righties allowed you to use plenty of left-handed hitters at the top of the order, something that the team has in abundance.
The best right-handed hitter on the roster without Judge is hard to pinpoint, especially since all of them are significantly worse against same-handed pitching. Heliot Ramos might just be the best option to bat highest among them, which would be cleanup in this scenario.
It's not an ideal situation in the slightest. Even if you don't think it makes sense to bat Ramos that high because of his struggles against righties, there is some merit to breaking up the team's many left-handed bats. In a lineup that will likely only feature one other righty, it has to be considered.
The fate of this lineup when they're out there, which would likely be mostly after a potential Wild Card Series with the Red Sox, would hinge on the middle. Spencer Jones and Jazz Chisholm Jr. got hot in August and helped the offensive turnaround begin, but both are heavily streaky bats with contact issues. If they go cold, this lineup might limp through games like they did in July.
What the playoff lineup should look like against left-handed pitching
- Paul Goldschmidt (1B)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Ben Rice (DH)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- Anthony Volpe/José Caballero (3B)
- Austin Wells (C)
Here's where it gets interesting. How far do you lean into the platoons on a team with several players designated to specifically hit lefties, especially against a team that will likely lean heavily on those types of pitchers in Boston?
Many Yankees fans believe that it would be improper to take a guy like García, who is likely the team's second-best pound-for-pound hitter with Judge injured, out of the lineup, but you don't really have a choice here. He's slashing just .238/.274/.363 against lefties, while Goldschmidt has been among the team's best hitters against them for the last two seasons. Add in Rice's improvements against same-handed pitching, and it just needs to be done.
Using him in a different position is also just not happening. He has not played second base, where he was extremely poor, since 2025. The only position he's played this season is first base. If he wasn't so dreadful out there, maybe he could replace Chisholm, a mediocre hitter against lefties in his own right.
Speaking of defense, you might notice the lack of Amed Rosario, and that's intentional. Rosario's use on this roster was almost exclusively predicated on his ability to hit left-handed pitching, but he's been significantly worse at it this season. Add in his truly dreadful defense, and you have a conundrum.
Anthony Volpe is a better hitter than José Caballero, but there are questions about how his arm strength would play at third, where he's also very inexperienced with just three games played in Triple-A. Caballero would probably get the nod here, but he's someone who just plays better off the bench with his speed and versatility.
It's also an aggressive placement for Lombard, batting fifth in his first career playoff game. The results haven't quite been there yet for him, but he's always been significantly better against lefties and should be slid up the lineup and be treated as one of those platoon bats who are there to hit that handedness, even if it might lead to consequences in the bullpen.
Boston is loaded with left-handed pitching from the rotation to the bullpen, so there will be few opportunities to get to a guy like García on the bench. The rest of the bench would be situational with pinch runners and pinch hitters.
Things ultimately look particularly shallow, but is there a chance that some last-minute reinforcements could help out?
Could Trent Grisham or Giancarlo Stanton return to provide relief?
It seems unlikely, especially early in the postseason, but the Yankees are refusing to shut the door on either Trent Grisham's or Giancarlo Stanton's return.
Grisham, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain earlier this month, was revealed to be "pretty far along" in his running program, and Boone said it's not out of the question that he returns in the season's final days, although an exact timeline for that has not been spelled out. If Grisham is physically ready to get back on the field, it would provide a boost, even if he might not be starting over Jones at this point.
Stanton, who's been out since April due to two separate calf strains and a re-aggravation, has continued to hit through his rehab, but hasn't resumed running as of last Sunday. Considering how it took several weeks for him to even get close to back from injury with his running program last time, this likely doesn't put him in play until the ALCS at the earliest.
While Stanton seems significantly less likely to get into a game again this season, there is a path for Grisham. The team could use him and Ramos in a platoon situation to add yet another lefty to the lineup against right-handed pitching. They could also utilize him as a pinch hitter on a larger bench than usual, due to the team's propensity to carry fewer than 13 pitchers in the Wild Card Series.
The real question for Grisham is defensive. While Jones has absolutely looked shaky in center field, the struggles of Grisham out there are well documented. Add in his diminished athleticism and likely balky hamstring straight off an injury, would it be better if the team just chanced it by throwing him in right field when he plays?
He hasn't played the position since a disastrous error lost the Brewers the 2019 Wild Card Game against the Nationals, but playing it at Yankee Stadium is significantly easier than dealing with the spacious center field. Of course, this is something the Yankees would have to determine their willingness to do beforehand and have him practice the position, so what plans they have will be determined by that.
As for Stanton if he's ever medically able to get back? There just might not be any room for him with Rice as the permanent DH. You don't want to take the bat out of either of their hands, and with the team seemingly having to juggle multiple guys coming off soft-tissue injuries, can they afford to use a roster spot for a designated pinch hitter as they did with 2022 Matt Carpenter?

item.title: [heavy.com] Cardinals Receive Strong Message Involving Yankees' Anthony Volpe

item.content:encoded:
The St. Louis Cardinals missed the playoffs this season and will need to head back to the drawing board to build a team that can qualify for the postseason next year.
Moreover, the question is what moves they should make to improve the team to challenge the Chicago Cubs and Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Central.
It’s been a wild 2026 MLB season for Anthony Volpe, who was optioned to Triple-A in August and then recalled in September. Still, it might be in the 25-year-old’s best interest to get a fresh start elsewhere.
Since reaching the majors in 2023, Volpe has been hitting .225 with 432 hits, 54 homers, 218 RBIs, and 241 runs scored in 537 games for the New York Yankees in his career, per StatMuse.
Despite this production during his four seasons in Pinstripes, FanSided’s Robert Murray believes that the Cardinals could be the change of scenery that Volpe needs after a rollercoaster career with the Yankees.
“Anthony Volpe would be a really good, buy-low option for the Cardinals,” Murray wrote in a Sept. 19 article. “Volpe was supposed to be the Yankees’ long-term answer at shortstop. Instead, he struggled mightily and fluctuated between the majors and minors.
“The Yankees still believe in Volpe and want to hold him, so a trade might be considered unlikely. But this is something that other teams will sniff around this offseason, I believe, and Bloom – who has previously worked with the Red Sox and Rays – should have plenty of familiarity in dealing with the Yankees.”
Anthony Volpe Could Boost Trade Value In the Coming Weeks
Since being recalled on Sept. 9, Volpe has performed well. Entering Sept. 20, Volpe has been batting .290 with nine hits, a home run, seven RBIs, and four runs scored in seven games, per StatMuse.
Moreover, if Volpe can end the season on a high note and have a productive postseason, his trade value might increase, and a team like the Cardinals could feel they can tap into his potential.
Volpe will have an opportunity to step up like every Yankee in that lineup, given that Aaron Judge is back on the injured list. New York can’t replace Judge with one batter, but they can do so with everyone chipping in.
Cardinals, Yankees Get Compelling Trade Idea
Recently, Christopher Kline of FanSided floated a trade idea that would send Volpe along with LHP Brent Headrick and LHP Kyle Carr to the Cardinals for 24-year-old shortstop Masyn Winn.
“The Yankees’ lack of fundamental soundness on the defensive end has bitten them in the you-know-what all season, just like it did last year,” Kline wrote in a Sept. 16 article. “The hope was that top prospect George Lombard Jr. could steady the ship at shortstop, but he has stacked up errors left and right.
“It’s too early to write off the 21-year-old long term, but he could serve more comfortably at third or second — which is notable, since Jazz Chisholm Jr. is about to [be a free agent]. Winn immediately alleviates a ton of defensive issues for the Yankees, while his weaker bat would be well-protected in the American League’s most potent lineup.”

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees fell in heartbreaking fashion on Saturday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers, losing on a walk-off two-run shot from Pavin Smith.
New York is now 89-65 on the season and still sits firmly in the top Wild Card spot but trails the Tampa Bay Rays by five games for the AL East division.
Currently, the biggest concern for the Yankees stems from injuries, as Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. are all sidelined. Even rookie slugger Spencer Jones seems to be dealing with some type of foot injury.
Aaron Boone Makes Statement on Jones’ Decision
Fortunately, Jones’ injury does not seem serious as he said pregame it was “no big deal.”
In fact, Boone said that he was available off the bench during Saturday night’s game and ultimately explained why he didn’t use him as a pinch-hitter.
After a reporter asked Boone if Jones was available or if he was trying to stay away from him because of the injury, Boone made it clear that he would’ve gone to him if the right spot emerged.
“He was available, like I would’ve… if a spot came up to hit or we needed to do something I would’ve gone to him,” Boone said.
Aaron Boone speaks to the media following the Yankees 5-3 loss tonight in Arizona. pic.twitter.com/aeBBxybvHN
— YES Network (@YESNetwork) September 20, 2026
Looking at the Yankees
New York will play the Diamondbacks one more time on Sunday and then, after a day off Monday, will begin a massive four-game set with the Rays. If they can sweep the series, they could get back into the race over the final three games of the regular season.
On Tuesday, the two teams will play a doubleheader and then wrap it up across Wednesday and Thursday, with the Yankees likely throwing their top four guys in Max Fried, Carlos Rodon, Gerrit Cole, and Cam Schlittler.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — In case the Yankees weren’t dealing with enough injury headaches for a 6-foot-7 slugger, Spencer Jones was out of the lineup Saturday with a sore left foot/heel.
The rookie outfielder claimed it was “no big deal” and chalked it up to the wear and tear of playing on Chase Field’s turf Friday night after jamming his heel in Minnesota earlier this week.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
But after the Yankees just lost Aaron Judge to the injured list again with a right calf strain, the last thing they needed was Jones nursing an injury of his own.
“Just a little banged up,” Jones said before Saturday’s game against the Diamondbacks. “Playing on turf is different, hard on the feet.”
Aaron Boone also downplayed it, adding that he still almost kept Jones in the lineup before sitting him in favor of José Caballero, who started in center field for the second time this season.
“Just felt like especially being on the turf here, he kind of jammed that heel in Minnesota and being on the turf [Friday], so I think it’s just a day-to-day kind of thing,” Boone said. “I even view him as available tonight.”
Boone said he preferred to keep Cody Bellinger in left field instead of shifting him to center.
“I considered moving him to center, but Belli’s grinding too and the turf here kind of beats you up,” he said. “There’s some scenarios where I would move him to center. Tonight, just being on the turf and as much as he’s been through this year, I didn’t want to move him.”
When the Yankees officially placed Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday, they opted for defensive versatility over offensive upside in his replacement.
That meant calling up Max Schuemann instead of Jasson Domínguez, giving the former another shot in the big leagues for at least a few days beginning this weekend against the Diamondbacks.
“Adding his versatility to our bench makes some sense,” Boone said. “And then obviously some different roster complications moving forward with the playoffs around the corner.”
Schuemann’s stay may be brief, with Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially returning from the IL as soon as the upcoming series against the Rays at Yankee Stadium that begins Tuesday.
If Schuemann goes back to Triple-A to make room, he would not be available to be recalled for 10 days (unless he was replacing an injured player again), essentially ruling him out as an option for the AL wild-card series.
That may have played a part in Domínguez not getting the call this time, in case the Yankees wanted to use him as a pinch-running threat on their playoff roster.
The 23-year-old also offers value as a switch-hitter, but he has proven to be a defensive liability in the outfield.
The Yankees’ trip to Chase Field gave them a chance to reunite with former teammate Jonathan Loáisiga, who has finally stayed healthy for a full season in the Diamondbacks bullpen.
Shop Yankees Merch
The right-hander often flashed his talent during his eight-year tenure with the Yankees, but injuries too often got in the way.
This season, though, after signing a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks, Loáisiga has avoided the IL and pitched in a career-high 64 games with a 2.32 ERA entering Saturday.
“Been through a lot of battles over the years with Jonny,” Boone said. “It’ll be great to see him. Hopefully we can ding him a little bit here. I know he’s had a really strong year, which I’m excited about for him. He’s such a talented guy that for him, it’s always been about just being healthy. So the fact that he’s gone out there and had a largely healthy season, I’m not surprised at the success he’s had.”
The Diamondbacks held a 25th-anniversary celebration Saturday of their 2001 World Series team that beat the Yankees in seven games.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] How the Yankees Should Utilize Jazz Chisholm Jr. When He Returns
item.dc:creator: Joe Najarian; Unknown
item.description: With Aaron Judge likely done for the season, the New York Yankees will rely heavily on their other bats to pick up the slack. One of those will be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is nearing a return from the injured list with a sprained right thumb. Chisholm, who was putting up an .832 OPS and .367 wOBA since August 4, is expected to be activated during the Yankees' final homestand this coming week. Despite a very disappointing season as a whole, the 28-year-old's improved play is an extremely encouragin
item.content:encoded:
With Aaron Judge likely done for the season, the New York Yankees will rely heavily on their other bats to pick up the slack.
One of those will be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is nearing a return from the injured list with a sprained right thumb. Chisholm, who was putting up an .832 OPS and .367 wOBA since August 4, is expected to be activated during the Yankees' final homestand this coming week. Despite a very disappointing season as a whole, the 28-year-old's improved play is an extremely encouraging sign.
At the same time, Anthony Volpe has taken full advantage of his new opportunity at second base. When Chisholm went down, Volpe's improvements at the plate in Triple-A carried over to the major leagues and his production from the bottom of the order is a boon to the Yankees' offense. The 25-year old is slashing .296/.345/.481 in 29 plate appearances while also stealing four bases.
The problem is that the Yankees have three middle infielders looking for starting spots. George Lombard Jr. is firmly entrenched at shortstop, which necessitated Volpe's transition to second base. Of course, second base is Chisholm's natural position and the Yankees have gotten well-above average defense from him there.
This means one of these three will be the odd man out... or does it?
The Yankees should play Jazz Chisholm Jr. at third base again
When the Yankees acquired Chisholm at the trade deadline in 2024, they already had Gleyber Torres at second base. So they tested Chisholm out at third base to ensure both players would be in the starting lineup. Chisholm also saw time at the hot corner last year when DJ LeMahieu played second, until the Yankees eventually released the aging LeMahieu to move Chisholm back to his natural position.
Chisholm's defense suffered at third in 2025, as he was worth -3 Outs Above Average (per Baseball Savant). But his athleticism and dynamic skillset is far too great to leave him out of the lineup entirely, even if he's endured a down year. On the other hand, it would be foolish for the Yankees to sit Volpe while he's hot at the plate and adapting well to second.
While second base has two strong options, third base is a major weakness. Ryan McMahon has been atrocious since returning to the lineup on Sept. 1, hitting just .154/.214/.179 in 42 plate appearances; the abysmal offensive production far outweighs McMahon's steady defense, even if the Yankees are going to rely on run prevention in the postseason. Jose Caballero is also capable of playing third, but he's best suited as a bench player at this point.
Between Chisholm and Volpe, the former is better suited to play third due to his past experience. The latter has a grand total of three games and 22.0 innings at the hot corner, all of them in Triple-A.
This certainly isn't an ideal situation for Chisholm: he's struggled for much of the season, got injured when he started turning things around, and may need to play at a secondary position to accommodate a teammate.
But this would likely be the Yankees' best lineup without Aaron Judge, and if Chisholm wants to both win a World Series and secure a future in the Bronx, then moving over to third is the best thing he can do to help the team right now.
Joe Najarian is a writer for Yankees On SI, having previously covered the Yankees both for SI and additional sites since 2023. He also served as Deputy Editor for the Yankees, Mets and Orioles On SI sites, and additionally contributes to Athlon Sports and Men’s Journal covering Major League Baseball and other trending sports news. Joe is a graduate of Rutgers University in 2022, earning a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Media Studies.
Follow JoeNajarian

item.title: [CBS Sports] Three questions for Aaron Judge and the Yankees as injury casts doubt on slugger's playoff availability
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa

item.content:encoded:
Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). Captain Aaron Judge is less than two weeks after returning from a fractured rib that sidelined him more than three months. Judge's status for the rest of the season is up in the air.
"I don't have a timeline on him. I'm not going to predict anything. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires," manager Aaron Boone said (via MLB.com). "... The reality is, we've had to play a lot of the season this year without him. There's no replacing a player who is as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations. Those don't change now."
The Yankees are always cagey about Judge's injuries. They declined to reveal the severity of the calf strain or give a timetable for his return. Generally speaking, Grade 1 calf strains (the least severe) require 2-3 weeks on the injured list, though calves are very tricky and easy to reinjury. They must be allowed to heal fully, otherwise you risk a more severe injury.
For all intents and purposes, the Yankees are locked into the top wild-card spot. They're six games up in the loss column on the Boston Red Sox, who currently sit in the second wild card spot, plus the Yankees won the season series and have the tiebreaker, so it's really a seven-game lead. New York can clinch the top wild-card spot as soon as Sunday.
The AL East title remains mathematically possible, but it is a long shot. The Yankees are four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the loss column with four head-to-head games remaining next week in the Bronx. The Rays only need to win one of those four games to clinch the season series and secure the tiebreaker, upping the difficulty for New York.
Just to lay it all out, here's what needs to happen for the Yankees to win the AL East, assuming they sweep those four games against the Rays and clinch the tiebreaker for themselves, which is a pretty big assumption:
- Rays go 6-3 or better: Rays win AL East
- Rays go 5-4: Yankees must go 9-0
- Rays go 4-5: Yankees must go 8-1
- Rays go 3-6: Yankees must go 7-2
- Rays go 2-7: Yankees must go 6-3
- Rays go 1-8: Yankees must go 5-4
- Rays go 0-9: Yankees must go 4-5
The Yankees have already clinched a postseason spot and winning the AL East was a long shot even with Judge. These last nine regular-season games are almost meaningless. If the AL East race gets interesting in a few days, the Yankees can shift gears, but the big picture takes priority this next week. Resting key relievers, lining up the rotation for the Wild Card Series, etc.
"Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he's the best hitter in the game," Cody Bellinger said (via MLB.com). "For us in here, our mindset is, we're going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I'm fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody."
With the postseason less than two weeks away, Judge's calf injury creates a lot of questions for both him and the Yankees overall. Here are three questions for the man himself, and his team.
Three questions for Judge
1. Will he return for the postseason? This is really the only question, right? The Yankees are built around Judge being the best hitter in the world, and when he's not, the walls begin to cave in. New York had one of the lowest-scoring offenses in baseball when Judge was out with his rib injury. To paraphrase another New York baseball legend, Judge is the straw that stirs the drink.
Judge is eligible to come off the injured list next Sunday, the final day of the regular season. Roster-wise, he can return in time for the postseason. Health-wise, we have no idea. Calf strains are rarely 10-day absences, but that's what the Yankees have to hope is the case here. There's a very real chance the Yankees are without Judge for at least the Wild Card Series, and maybe longer.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason,” Aaron Judge said. “That’s definitely the plan.”
Said the calf strain involves the soleus muscle — which he said is more crucial to running and hitting — making it more difficult to play through.
2. Will he be himself at the plate? Judge did not go on a minor-league rehab assignment before returning from the rib injury and it showed. He went 4 for 23 (.174) with one walk and 13 strikeouts in his seven games back before the calf injury. His timing was not there at all. Judge's one homer came on a hanging breaking ball. Otherwise, pitchers threw fastballs by him consistently.
To put a number on it, Judge missed with 41% of his swings against fastballs in his seven games back, more than double the 19% league average. This is what it looks like when you miss with more than two out of every five swings against heaters:
It is not exactly a surprise a hitter who did not go on a rehab assignment after spending more than three months on the shelf looked out of sorts at the plate. Judge and the Yankees knew it would take him some time to get back up to speed at the plate, and they were willing to live with it. The goal was always to be ready for the postseason, not so much the regular season.
These last nine games aren't particularly important for the Yankees in the standings, but they were incredibly important to Judge. He needed at-bats to rediscover his timing at the plate, and get back to being the dominant hitter he's been throughout his career. The calf strain puts that on pause. Judge now has even fewer at-bats available to get back to being himself.
3. Will he be able to play the field? There is a scenario in which Judge plays through the calf strain as a full-time DH who doesn't run at 100% (or close to it). How the Yankees would align their defense in that scenario, I have no idea. Ben Rice is a full-time DH these days and also New York's best non-Judge hitter. Platoon-mates Luis Gárcia Jr. and Paul Goldschmidt are first basemen.
Unless the Yankees do something unexpected, like put Gárcia back at second base (where he was terrible defensively) or Rice back behind the plate (where he was also terrible defensively), slotting Judge in at DH means one of the team's most productive hitters will have to sit. This is something the Yankees will worry about when the time comes, and not a second sooner.
Three questions for the Yankees
1. Where will the righty pop come from? The Yankees have a very lefty-heavy lineup and Judge's righty heft provides important balance. Only the Cleveland Guardians have gotten fewer plate appearances from righties this season. Friday's lineup against Arizona Diamondbacks lefty Eduardo Rodriguez could be what the Yankees run out there against lefties in October:
- 1B Paul Goldschmidt, RHB
- LF Cody Bellinger, LHB
- RF Heliot Ramos, RHB
- DH Ben Rice, LHB
- 3B Amed Rosario, RHB
- CF Spencer Jones, LHB
- SS George Lombard Jr., RHB
- C Austin Wells, LHB
- 2B Anthony Volpe, RHB
Goldschmidt and Ramos are lefty mashers. Bellinger and Rice are very productive left-on-left hitters. Jones has performed well against lefties as a big leaguer, though his minor-league track record against southpaws isn't great. Rosario is having his worst season against lefties. The 7-8-9 spots are unlikely to make an impact offensively, regardless of the pitcher's handedness.
That lineup would look much more imposing with Judge in the No. 3 spot. Perhaps this is not such a big concern though? Since trade deadline day, the Yankees have the highest batting average (.289) and on-base percentage (.362) against lefties, and the third-highest slugging percentage (.456) despite Judge not playing much, and not being much of a factor when he did play.
In all likelihood the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, and Boston has three quality lefty starters (Jake Bennett, Ranger Suárez, Payton Tolle) and a shutdown lefty relief tandem (Aroldis Chapman, Erik Miller). To beat the Red Sox, the Yankees will need their righty hitters to produce, and now the status of their best right-handed hitter is in question.
2. Will the pitching hold up? Despite not having Judge for more than three months, the Yankees have the American League's best run differential (+143) and second-best record (89-64). They can thank their pitching staff. New York has allowed only 3.68 runs per game this year, the fewest in baseball. Since trade deadline day, it's an incredible 3.37 runs allowed per game.
There are some cracks beginning to form, however. Gerrit Cole has surrendered eight home runs in his last three starts, including five on a four-seam fastball that is no longer the dominant pitch it was at his peak. Max Fried's velocity has been down a tick since returning from a bone bruise in his elbow late last month. That injury has sent him to the injured list twice this year.
Cam Schlittler, the AL Cy Young favorite, has thrown a career-high 184 ⅔ innings with two regular-season starts remaining, plus the postseason. Key late-inning relievers Paul Blackburn, David Bednar, and Brent Headrick have worked a lot -- A LOT -- this season and have all shown a slight dip in velocity in recent weeks, which perhaps is a sign the workload is catching up to them.
Without Judge (and sometimes even with him), the Yankees are a run prevention team. Their superpower is a suffocating pitching staff that is among the best in baseball at limiting hard contact, particularly in the air. With Judge absent, the pitching staff and the ability to prevent runs in general will be of paramount importance. No Judge reduces the margin of error considerably.
3. What about their other injured players? Judge is not the only injured Yankee. Center field Trent Grisham has not played since Sept. 4 due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain. On Friday, Boone said Grisham is pretty far into his running program, and he could make it back before the end of the regular season. That would give the outfield a lift should Judge miss extended time.
Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. has not played since jamming his thumb sliding into second base on Sept. 8. Boone said Chisholm will come off the injured list when the Yankees return home next week. He's had a down year overall, but Chisholm was playing his best baseball of the season right before the injury. He's an important presence given his speed and defense in particular.
Left-hander Ryan Weathers is working his way back from a flexor strain. He last pitched Aug. 22. Weathers is throwing bullpen sessions, though Boone confirmed he won't return during the regular season. If/when Weathers does return, it will be as a reliever. He has bullpen experience and the Yankees could use middle relief help, but Weathers has to make it back first.
At minimum, Chisholm and Grisham would give the Yankees more options for their Judge-less lineup, even if they only platoon. It wouldn't be hard to find a role for Weathers, who had allowed no more than one run in six of his last seven starts before the injury. Bottom line though, the Yankees need Judge. Everything else is secondary to his return and effectiveness.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees were dealt another major injury blow earlier this week, and it came at the worst possible time in the MLB season.
Days later, on Saturday, the team placed Aaron Judge officially back on the injured list with a right calf strain, just 11 days after returning from a lengthy absence caused by a fractured rib.
At the same time, however, the Yankees received encouraging news on Jazz Chisholm Jr., who could be back in the lineup before the end of the regular season.
Aaron Judge heads back to injured list
Sep 11, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees right fielder Aaron Judge (99) runs back to the dugout in the sixth inning against the New York Mets at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The Yankees announced Saturday that Judge was placed on the 10-day injured list, retroactive to Sept. 17, with a right calf strain. New York recalled infielder/outfielder Max Schuemann from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre to take his roster spot.
Judge first experienced tightness in his lower right leg during Wednesday's game against the Minnesota Twins and was removed after the sixth inning. An MRI performed Thursday revealed the calf strain.
The bigger concern is the timing. Judge only returned Sept. 8 after missing more than three months with his rib injury. He went 4-for-23 with one home run across six games following his return.
Manager Aaron Boone has not provided a timetable for Judge's return and would not speculate about whether he will be available for the postseason. His earliest possible return is Sept. 27, the final day of the regular season.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. could return next week
Jun 2, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) walks off the field after the top of the seventh inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The Yankees did receive some positive injury news regarding Chisholm, who has been sidelined with a sprained right thumb since Sept. 10.
Boone said Chisholm is "doing well" and should be activated during the team's current homestand. MLB reports that Chisholm has hit for four consecutive days and has also resumed throwing, putting him on track for a potential return around Sept. 22-24.
That would give the Yankees a much-needed boost, particularly with Judge now sidelined again. New York is chasing Tampa Bay in the AL East and has a crucial four-game series against the Rays next week.
The Yankees now face the difficult task of navigating the final stretch of the regular season without their captain while hoping Chisholm can return as expected.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Últimas Noticias Sobre Las Lesiones De Los Yankees: Dos Jugadores Se Perderán El Resto De La Temporada Y Otros Dos Están A Punto De Volver
item.dc:creator: Esteban Quiñones

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — La lista de lesionados en el vestuario de los Yankees cuenta dos historias a la vez. Por un lado, se está vaciando. Por el otro, acaba de llenarse más. El mismo fin de semana en que dos titulares se acercaban a su regreso, el equipo se enteró de que terminaría la temporada regular sin su capitán.
Para unos Yankees que persiguen el título de división y se preparan para octubre, este momento tiene sus pros y sus contras. Llegan refuerzos tanto para el cuadro como para los jardines. Pero no volverán una pieza clave de la defensa ni un pilar de la rotación de lanzadores.
Chisholm y Grisham, a punto de volver
La buena noticia viene del lado de los jugadores de campo. Jazz Chisholm Jr., de baja desde el 10 de septiembre por un esguince en el pulgar derecho, volverá al equipo durante la serie en casa que empieza el martes contra los Rays. Boone dijo que Chisholm había bateado cuatro días seguidos y que ya había vuelto a lanzar.
Chisholm estaba en racha cuando se lesionó: había promediado un promedio de bateo de 0,375, con un porcentaje de embasado de 0,464 y un jonrón en sus últimos siete partidos. Su regreso devuelve a los Yankees a su segunda base titular justo en el momento más importante de la temporada.
«Veremos cuáles son nuestras necesidades y cómo se le ve, y si creemos que está listo para incorporarse y aportar su granito de arena», dijo Boone.
Grisham le sigue de cerca. El jardinero central lleva fuera desde el 5 de septiembre por una distensión de grado 2 en el isquiotibial derecho, y Boone ha dicho que ya está muy avanzado en su programa de recuperación con carreras. Ahora los Yankees barajan la posibilidad de que vuelva antes de que termine la temporada regular.
Judge, de baja por una distensión en la pantorrilla
La noticia más impactante es la de Aaron Judge. El tres veces MVP de la Liga Americana entra en la lista de lesionados de 10 días por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, una decisión que los Yankees hicieron oficial el sábado, aunque con efecto retroactivo desde el jueves. Así que su regreso más temprano podría ser en el último partido de la temporada regular, el 27 de septiembre.
Judge tuvo que abandonar el partido del miércoles, que acabaron perdiendo en la 13.ª entrada en Minnesota, por una contractura en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha, que, según él, empezó ya en la primera entrada. Una resonancia magnética realizada el jueves en Phoenix confirmó la distensión. Boone no quiso dar detalles sobre la gravedad ni sobre el tiempo de recuperación, y tampoco se comprometió a que volviera para la postemporada.
Cuando le preguntaron directamente si Judge volvería para los playoffs, Boone fue breve.
«No lo sé», dijo Boone. «No tengo un plazo para él. Ahora mismo está en la lista de lesionados. No voy a hacer predicciones. Está recibiendo tratamiento y ya veremos qué pasa».
Su ausencia se nota menos de lo que se habría notado antes. Los Yankees tienen un balance de 48-39 en los partidos que Judge se ha perdido esta temporada y de 41-25 cuando juega. Aun así, Boone se lo puso claro sobre la derrota.
«No hay quien pueda sustituir a un jugador tan bueno como Aaron Judge, pero tenemos grandes expectativas», dijo Boone. «Y eso no va a cambiar ahora».
A Weathers se le acaba la pista
El contratiempo más discreto es el de Ryan Weathers. El zurdo lleva en la lista de lesionados desde el 23 de agosto por una distensión en los flexores del antebrazo izquierdo, y Boone admitió el viernes que es poco probable que lance en un partido antes de que termine la temporada.
Esto descarta que el lanzador, que sin hacer mucho ruido se había convertido en uno de los brazos más fiables de los Yankees, vuelva a jugar esta temporada regular. Weathers terminó con un balance de 5-8 y una efectividad de 3,60 en 25 salidas como titular —su mejor marca personal—, y registró una efectividad de 2,27 en sus últimas siete salidas antes de la lesión.
No está totalmente descartado para lo que queda de temporada. Weathers tenía previsto hacer una segunda sesión de bullpen el sábado, y el siguiente paso sería una sesión de bateo en vivo. Todavía es posible que tenga un papel en el bullpen durante la postemporada si su preparación avanza más rápido, aunque los Yankees esperarán para valorar su progreso.
La estadística que cambia el panorama del jardín
El regreso de Trent Grisham parecía complicado antes de que Judge se lesionara, porque el novato Spencer Jones aprovechó la oportunidad. Jones ha bateado .361, con un porcentaje de embasado de .425 y un porcentaje de slugging de .528 en los 10 partidos que lleva jugando en el centro del campo.
La ausencia de Judge cambia las cuentas. Ahora hay sitio para los dos. Grisham podría volver a jugar de centro frente a los lanzadores diestros, lo que dejaría a Jones en el campo derecho, donde de otro modo estaría Judge. Una lesión ha creado discretamente un hueco en la alineación que no existía hace una semana.
El jugador de campo interior y exterior Max Schuemann se ha desplazado a Phoenix para unirse a los Yankees de cara al partido del sábado, aportando profundidad al equipo mientras se va definiendo la alineación.
El martes empieza en el Yankee Stadium una serie de cuatro partidos contra los Rays, que incluye una doble jornada, y que podría decidir el título de la división. Los Yankees la afrontarán sin Judge ni Weathers, pero probablemente con Chisholm y quizá Grisham de vuelta en el equipo.
Por ahora, el panorama es mitad optimista, mitad sombrío. Dos jugadores vuelven a cruzar la puerta del vestuario. Otros dos están pendientes del calendario, con la esperanza de que aún haya tiempo para marcar la diferencia en octubre.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario abajo.

The Yanks scored five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks in the first game of a weekend series Friday, and the teams meet again Saturday in Phoenix as Arizona attempts to stay alive in the National League wild-card race. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees will play the rest of the regular season without slugger Aaron Judge. While they understand the magnitude of his loss, they enter the stretch run with belief.
The Yanks scored five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks in the first game of a weekend series Friday, and the teams meet again Saturday in Phoenix as Arizona attempts to stay alive in the National League wild-card race.
"Obviously losing 'Judgey' hurts," Cody Bellinger said. "We all know he's the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is we're going to have to find a way. The talent in this room speaks for itself.
"I'm fully confident we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win and beat anybody."
American League Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) will face Arizona right-hander Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) in the second game of the series.
The Diamondbacks (80-74) will ask Pfaadt to end a slump in which they have lost five of six. They are five games behind San Diego, the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia (all 85-69) for the three NL wild-card spots with eight games to play.
"We know where we're at," Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said. "We can't afford to worry about things we can't control. I'm going to say there's time. There's always time."
The Yankees (89-64) are 48-39 this season without Judge, who was placed on the injured list Friday with a strained right calf after missing three months earlier with a fractured right rib.
New York is also without injured regulars Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb) and Trent Grisham (hamstring), although manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm could return for the Tampa Bay series early next week.
The Yankees, who already have qualified for the postseason, are four games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East, and the teams have a four-game series at Yankee Stadium beginning Tuesday.
"There is no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations that don't change now," Boone said. "One thing we do know is that we are in the dance.
"We've been built on the strength of our starting pitching all year."
No one has been as strong as Schlittler, who is in his first full season and has made every start while Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon have missed time with injuries or recovery time.
Schlittler has won four of his last five starts and has given up one run or fewer in each of his last seven. He was struck on the back of his right leg by Bo Bichette's 111.5 mph comebacker on his 94th and last pitch of a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets last Sunday, but shrugged it off.
"You have an ace at the top that has pitched like that," Boone said. "That's a good place to start. He's been dominant. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch last year."
Schlittler has never faced the Diamondbacks, although Jesus Sanchez is 4 for 12 with three walks against him.
Pfaadt is 0-2 with a 5.74 ERA in his last five starts, and he gave up six runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings in a loss to Texas on Aug. 12. He will be pitching on six days' rest after being pushed back so Eduardo Rodriguez could start the first game of the series.
Pfaadt lost his only outing against the Yankees, giving up six runs in 4 1/3 innings of a 7-1 loss as a rookie in 2023. Cody Bellinger is 2 for 7 with two solo homers against him and Luis Garcia Jr. is 3 for 7 with a homer.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Are Creating Their Own Distraction With Aaron Judge Injury Secrecy
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
item.description: The New York Yankees haven't exactly been forthright about what's been going on with Aaron Judge. They didn't offer much information when he was initially pulled during the game against the Minnesota Twins. All the public knew was that Judge had tightness in his lower leg, and that was about it. They didn't alleviate any concerns about Judge after he was placed on the injured list. In fact, things have been just as hush. According to the Daily News' Gary Phillips, Judge wasn't available to speak
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees haven't exactly been forthright about what's been going on with Aaron Judge. They didn't offer much information when he was initially pulled during the game against the Minnesota Twins. All the public knew was that Judge had tightness in his lower leg, and that was about it.
They didn't alleviate any concerns about Judge after he was placed on the injured list. In fact, things have been just as hush.
According to the Daily News' Gary Phillips, Judge wasn't available to speak to the media before the game. He wasn't there for them after their 9-2 win against the Arizona Diamondbacks either. The extent of the calf strain is still unclear.
Aaron Boone didn't offer up much of an answer when asked about Judge. His response was muted and didn't offer insight into whether he'll return in the postseason.
"I don't have a timeline on him," Boone said, according to MLB.com's Bryan Hoch. "I'm not going to predict anything. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires."
While the public knowing what's wrong with Judge doesn't change his schedule or the organization's plans heading into the postseason, their secrecy won't keep the team from answering a barrage of questions. In fact, they'll likely get more.
This isn't the type of story that goes away with time, and even though the Yankees beat a tough opponent in Eduardo Rodriguez, that will be the story on all the back pages. There won't be an image of a sullen Rodriguez walking off the mound, but rather an image of Judge plastered on every newspaper. This storm cloud is still following the team.
Ghosting the media is a weird look, too
Plus, Judge avoiding the media looks odd when Jazz Chisholm Jr. or Clint Frazier did the same and took hits for it. When Frazier did it in 2019, a headline in The Athletic said that he "ghosted" reporters. There won't be any of that with Judge.
Not speaking to the media was held against those guys and used to say something about their character. For Judge, their captain, the same standard should apply. If he is going to be the example of how a New York Yankee should carry themselves, he should be front and center for reporters, as anyone else would be.
Obviously, Judge could talk, and the Yankees can offer a realistic timetable for what they think is happening, but that doesn't change his timeline. They'll still have to be without him, and guys like Spencer Jones will need to step up.
Still, come the postseason, it's probably better to mitigate any potential circus around the team. Playing in October is hard enough, and the team already gets enough attention during this time of year. No need to make things harder for themselves.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Jazz Chisholm Jr. Expected to Return for Yankees' Final Homestand Against Rays
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh

Manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm is expected to be activated from the 10-day injured list during New York's final regular-season homestand. The second baseman has continued making progress during hi
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are getting closer to having Jazz Chisholm Jr. back in the lineup.
Manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm is expected to be activated from the 10-day injured list during New York's final regular-season homestand. The Yankees begin that homestand Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Chisholm has been sidelined since Sept. 10 after spraining his right thumb on a head-first slide into second base against the Colorado Rockies.
The second baseman has continued making progress during his recovery. Boone said Friday marked Chisholm's fourth straight day of hitting in the batting cages, while he has also resumed throwing on the field.
The Yankees have been using Anthony Volpe at second base while Chisholm recovers. His return will give Boone another option in the infield as New York manages its lineup during the final week of the regular season.
Chisholm was also swinging the bat well before the injury. He hit .375 with a .464 on-base percentage and .500 slugging percentage over his final seven games.
The 28-year-old has appeared in 134 games this season, batting .232 with 16 doubles, three triples, 19 home runs and 55 RBI in 461 at-bats.
Chisholm has also provided plenty of value on the bases. He has scored 68 runs and stolen 40 bases on 49 attempts while posting a .312 on-base percentage and .403 slugging percentage.
His return comes at an important point for New York. The Yankees entered Saturday with an 88-64 record and sat 4 games behind the Rays in the AL East.
New York is also dealing with the expected absence of Aaron Judge for the remainder of the regular season, making Chisholm's return another potential boost for the lineup.
For now, the Yankees will continue monitoring Chisholm's thumb as he works toward activation. If he remains on schedule, he should be back during the final homestand before the postseason begins.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — While Friday wasn’t a positive day in terms of injury news for the Aaron Judge-less Yankees, Aaron Boone did say that the team can count on a reinforcement soon.
That would be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is expected to return from a sprained right thumb on the team’s upcoming and final homestand of the regular season. Boone said that Friday was the second baseman’s fourth day of hitting in a row. He’s also been throwing the last few days.
“He’s getting very close,” Boone said.
Chisholm previously said that he hoped to come off the injured list when the Yankees returned home from Arizona. He hurt his thumb while sliding into second base on Sept. 8.
Chisholm is an impending free agent in the midst of a disappointing season, but he had rounded into form before getting. He hit .295 with an .832 OPS, three home runs, 10 RBI and 10 stolen bases over his last 29 games. He also had a .391 OPS and a 1.028 OPS over his last 15 games.
The hope is that Chisholm can pick up where he left off, especially with Judge returning to the IL with a right calf strain.
Chisholm is hitting .232 with a .715 OPS, 19 home runs, 55 RBI and 40 steals overall.
GRISHAM ‘COULD BE IN PLAY’
Boone also said that Trent Grisham is pretty far into his running progression and “could be in play at the end of the season.” The center fielder suffered his second right hamstring strain of the season earlier this month.
Prior to that, Grisham hit .211 with a .703 OPS and 18 home runs. He’s also been one of the slowest and worst defensive center fielders in baseball the last two years.
With Grisham not producing on either side of the ball and Spencer Jones more than holding his own, the former was not guaranteed to start in the playoffs prior to Judge’s injury. Now, however, Grisham could play center while Jones handles right. The Yankees can also use Jones in center and Heliot Ramos is right against lefties.
WEATHERS WON’T RETURN BEFORE PLAYOFFS
While the Yankees had hoped otherwise, Aaron Boone said Ryan Weathers is “unlikely” to return before the end of the regular season. The left-handed starter, working his way back from a flexor strain as a reliever, is expected to throw his second bullpen session at Chase Field on Saturday.
Asked if the Yankees would be comfortable having Weathers’ first game off the IL come in the postseason, neither Boone nor pitching coach Matt Blake ruled the idea out.
“I don’t know if ‘comfortable’ is [the right word],” Blake said, “but it might be the course of action where he’s the best option even though he hasn’t pitched in the last three or four weeks.”

PHOENIX — Aaron Judge is on the injured list again, but the Yankees could get two key pieces back off of it by next week.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated on the upcoming homestand that begins Tuesday, Aaron Boone said Friday, after the second baseman landed on the IL last week with a right thumb sprain.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Friday marked his fourth day of hitting in a row after being shut down from baseball activities for about a week, while he has also been throwing the last couple of days.
“He’s getting very close,” Boone said before the Yankees’ 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
Trent Grisham, meanwhile, is “pretty far into his running progression” from a right hamstring strain and “doing well,” Boone said, putting him in position to be in play at the end of the regular season.
Before Judge’s calf strain, it was questionable whether there would be a lane for Grisham to get playing time if and when he returned.
But now it is possible he could return to center field at least against righties, bumping Spencer Jones to right field.
As for Ryan Weathers, the other Yankee trying to make it back in time for the playoffs (from a left forearm flexor strain), Boone acknowledged the lefty is “unlikely to get into a game before the end of the season.”
Weathers is set to throw a second bullpen session on Saturday, after which he could advance to facing hitters in live batting practice.
Whether that will give him enough time to show he should be part of the bullpen for the first round of the playoffs remains to be seen.
“We’ll see what our needs are and how he looks and if we feel like he’s ready to come in and be a contributor,” Boone said.
Anthony Volpe, who was back at second base, hit .348 with a .965 OPS and four steals in his first seven games since being called back up from Triple-A as an injury replacement for Chisholm.
He was 0-for-4 in Friday night’s win.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the New York Yankees are playing the first game of their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
They are coming off a series where they won two out of three games over the Minnesota Twins at Target Field.
New York Yankees Announced Chisholm Jr. Update
The Yankees continue to play without one of their best players, as Jazz Chisholm Jr. has been out since September 8 with an injury.
Ahead of Friday’s game, manager Aaron Boone shared the latest on the two-time MLB All-Star.
Bryan Hoch of MLB.com wrote: “Jazz Chisholm Jr. is “doing well” and should be activated on this homestand, Aaron Boone said.”
Before getting hurt, Chisholm Jr. had been batting .232 with 107 hits, 19 home runs, 55 RBIs, 68 runs and 40 stolen bases in 134 games.
MLB.com also wrote (on September 18): “Went on the IL on Sept. 10 and will have no baseball activities for 7-10 days. “Doing well,” Aaron Boone said Sept. 18, Chisholm’s fourth consecutive day of hitting. He has also been throwing.”
Looking At Chisholm Jr.
Chisholm Jr. is in the middle of his third season playing for the Yankees.
Prior to New York, he had spent the first 4.5 seasons of his career on the Miami Marlins.
In 2024, Chisholm Jr. helped the Yankees reach the World Series.
This winter, Chisholm Jr. will be among the most intriguing free agents to hit the market.
He will turn 29 in February.
Yankees On Friday
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East.
They have gone 88-64 in 152 games.
Following three games in Arizona, the Yankees will host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday.
